grammar.label: Tense and aspect ordering
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
Tense is indicated seperately from aspect in Vayrshemon. There are seven forms for each verb that communicate tense. Three indicate the past, one indicates the present and three indicate the future. Both the past and the future tense, unlike the present tense, can convey a range of temporal immediacy. An action is specified to have occured in a contextually dependant relative time frame. The frame of refernce for an action¾s tense is that which is considered normal for the action. (The distant past with regard to a geological process is distinct from the distant past with regard to a human life span or from a nuclear process like the decay of a specific radioactive isotope.) In this way an event that occured 10 years ago with regard to the invention of a micro electronic device may be described in the distant past tense but an event that occured 10 years ago with regard to the development of technology in western societies may be described in the immediate past tense even though both examples refer to the same event. 
The general form of the past and future tense is agnostic of temporal immediacy and simply conveys that an event does not occur in the present but that it occurs sometime in the past or sometime in the future. Greater specificity is possible by using the immediate or distant variant of the past and future tense. Tense is affixed before aspect and either of the two inflections can be absent but not both.

This is a new proposal, not an attested rule.

grammar.label: Dramatic literary grammar 0.8
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
Vayrshemon 0.8 — dramatic literary branch

Scope and ancestry
This branch develops the 0.7 construction-gloss language for All's Well That Ends Well. It is an authored continuation, not a claim that Shakespearean dialogue was already expressible in the surviving specimens. The original archive records and frozen 0.7 history remain available. Dictionary records distinguish archive adaptations, previously proposed forms, new compounds, and new roots. No machine-selected random syllables or English-token substitution is used. The editorial transcription is written in target order and compiled only after every word and inflection is declared.

Reading the four columns
The first column is Thimfora 79; the second contains exactly the same encoded characters in Transliteration 7. The third is a compact construction gloss in target order. The fourth preserves the supplied Folger English, including speakers and stage directions. Paragraph boundaries may divide a long speech for page fit; they do not authorize omitted lines or reassigned speakers. The source index retains original line ranges and source-file hash. Separator lines made only of equals signs are excluded. The work begins at ACT 1, with no imported cast list or front matter.

Order, case and reference
Neutral transitive clauses prefer object–subject–verb. An established subject may precede its object or nominal predicate when discourse continuity makes that natural. A focused object remains before the subject. Lexical subjects take -lÉy (nom.); direct objects and nominal predicates take -get (acc.). Unmarked pronouns are subjects; the new branch extends -get to their object forms instead of pretending to have deciphered every historical pronoun-chart cell. Titles, vocatives, headings and dictionary citation forms may be bare. Nominal juxtaposition in lists shares a finite predicate; a recoverable copula may be absent in balanced proverbial or antithetical clauses. These are licensed constructions, not arbitrary word shuffling.

Case endings remain on the noun head. Adjectives follow their heads and take ’mç in ordinary count modification. Predicative adjectives may be followed by the copula and receive predicate case when explicitly substantivized. The nominative ending contains a legacy Maxima-looking slot internally; this is a vowel identity, not an invitation to Unicode recasing. Ordinary prose capitals come from the named Maxima/Minima pairs.

Nominal classes and number
The earlier thing-class gßÑet’ remains available for explicit classification and emphatic introduction. In this dramatic branch, a dictionary noun's lexical class permits a bare classified noun with overt case. This deliberately extends the earlier restricted discourse deletion rule: dialogue does not require the same thing-class prefix on every new participant. The change applies only in 0.8, and does not reinterpret earlier test failures. Count plurality uses -un, dual -et, before case. Collective nouns and generic classes need not be pluralized when no separate individuals are asserted. Mass nouns do not receive a count plural unless a portion/type reading is intended. The speaker collective ly remains; lym is a newly proposed individuated we. English singular/plural is interpreted, not mechanically copied.

Possession and relations
A possessor is placed before its head with ’: rá’son-root, ly’life-root. Nested possessors scope inward from the left. The head alone receives outer case. For clarity, free genitive -’i or the linker i can replace a long bound chain. The bound construction generalizes the earlier ly’ forms. Spatial relations normally use adpositions; optional clitics -’tha (source/abl.), -’ni (location), -’ra (goal), -’rin (means) keep the noun phrase compact. These are new productive relations. The source's on/about and instrumental with/external-agent by distinctions survive as separate inherited lexical roots.

Tense, aspect, voice and mood
Retain root + tense + aspect: -ow- present, -iz- general past, -at- general future; -ya simple, -am progressive, -fu perfect. Thus a present perfect expresses a past event with a relevant present result, whereas an ordinary narrated past uses -izya. Past perfect is -izfu. The source's will is not automatically future: volition uses the desire verb or a modal, and proverbial futures may be generic predictions. Temporal remoteness remains available under the older rules but is not forced into each past event.

New voice suffixes precede tense: -im passive, -ar causative, -ir reflexive, -il reciprocal. Passive changes the promoted participant without inventing an agent; an expressed agent is introduced by Ëers. -e is a direct imperative. -’en marks a nonfinite complement; -’es a simultaneous or attendant-action converb. ef’ nominalizes an event, retaining the archived conversion family. Modal particles precede their scope: jor necessity, lah permission/possibility, jwën ability, ve irrealis. Unstressed postverbal ’jor, ’lah and ’jwën are permitted when the scope is the whole preceding predicate, especially in subordinate clauses. They do not duplicate a separately expressed modal. -’ve after a finite form marks irrealis; -’ne marks a wish or blessing. Negative ma precedes the constituent it denies; whole-clause negation is placed before the predicate/modal group. A positive imperative does not become negative merely by describing a bad action.

Questions, subordination and ellipsis
Clause-final ib closes polar questions; interrogatives retain the chart's semantic families: Ñetib thing, falib person, horib reason, kãnib manner, kÇnib location. ka introduces a content clause; ki a relative clause. A resumptive pronoun or explicit relation identifies the relative's role when a gap would be unclear. mßrnav introduces an open conditional, rav its optional consequent. Counterfactual tense/mood is expressed on the verb, not inferred from English if alone. vin is temporal when, vinel while, vinto until; kenst is because; venka although; maka lest. Lest already encodes avoidance and does not require an extra negative that would reverse its meaning.

An immediately continued subject can remain unspoken only while reference is secure. A new speaker, topic change, competing referent or contrast restores it. Dialogue answers can be fragments. Interrupted sentences remain interrupted: Parolles and Helena's broken exchange must not be repaired into assertions they never finish. A standalone at represents a suspended future auxiliary in that particular construction, not a general replacement for finite verbs.

People, register and address
Keep rá I, ly collective we, po inanimate it. This branch proposes ne respectful or plural you, nel familiar/downward singular you, zi he, za she, zem animate they, vem generic one, and lym individuated we. These are authored paradigms rather than purported transcriptions of the older chart. The English thou/you distinction guides social distance, but irony, intimacy and rank are considered in each exchange. arza, arzi and arvenek distinguish madam, sir and lord. Kinship terms can be literal or socially offered; Countess calling Helena daughter must not silently become a claim of biological parentage.

Word formation and lexical limits
Compounds are semantic proposals with their components recorded. They are not required to be fully transparent after lexicalization. New roots fill lexical gaps in bodily life, society and affect, while established verbs remain productive. Synonyms are chosen for meaning and voice, not to maximize a diversity statistic. Repeated words remain repeated when Shakespeare uses anaphora, mockery or an argument's key term. Names are adapted consistently, with original spellings visible in the English column. Unknown historical phonetic values remain unknown; the Roman font is authoritative for this edition's reading display, and dictionary text does not invent an IPA pronunciation for unresolved letters.

Numerals
Act/scene numbers in the range used here preserve their ordinary values. Larger source quantities preserve decimal meanings: ten means decimal 10 (the Unta eshna value), not the Unta written string 10, which would mean twelve. Mil names the source culture's decimal thousand. Conventional time units such as hour and year retain the source's intended duration. No rhetorical thousand is silently converted into a different quantity.

Gloss key
nom. subject; acc. object/predicate; dat. recipient; gen./poss. possessor; mod. postnominal modifier; adv. adverb; prs./pst./fut. tense; pf. perfect; prog. progressive; pass. passive; caus. causative; recp. reciprocal; refl. reflexive; imp. command; inf. nonfinite complement; cv. converb; opt. wish; irr. irrealis; pl./du. plural/dual; nmlz. event noun; th. explicit thing classification; abil./possib./necess. ability/possibility/necessity. A dot separates gloss words; hyphens expose a compound's lexical construction. Labels explain structure, not a claim of perfect word-for-word English equivalence.

Act II register refinements
Unmarked lexical subjects are also licensed in continuous dialogue when person, order and argument structure identify the subject without a rival reading. Full nominative marking restores a contrast, introduces a competing participant, or separates adjacent clauses. This is differential subject marking, not deletion of all case. Accusative remains especially useful on fronted objects. Noun compounds place their qualifying stem before the head; separate descriptive modifiers normally follow and use the modifier ending. A short finite modifier may precede a noun in a restrictive reading; ki remains the explicit relative boundary for longer or potentially ambiguous attachments.

The reduced generic ending -ya, without the present segment -ow-, is used for maxims and recurring dispositions: it does not locate a particular present event. The full -owya remains appropriate to an event now or a state asserted now. The distinction lets the King's maxims and the Fool's supposed general truths differ from immediate stage action without arbitrary synonym replacement.

Negative ma before a constituent has narrow scope. Clause-final ma is a dialogue variant with scope over the completed assertion, particularly a denial or correction; it does not reverse an embedded conditional. An overt negative beside a permission or necessity modal must be read with that modal's stated scope, not as a blanket equivalent of English cannot or must not. In the construction gloss, negation remains visible as its own word.

Productive zero conversion permits a root naming an action to name its event or result, and a state root to serve as a predicate adjective. Finite endings identify verbal use; case identifies nominal use. The dictionary groups the same written form's related senses rather than counting happy/happiness or know/known as invented separate words. Homophonous but unrelated senses are recorded separately within that headword and must not be conflated by a translator.

Lexicalization is explicit. The long newly composed contempt-speech expression is conventionalized as grënaw, scorn; zálinhifår is steward, and mermiktaz×r is navigator. These are 0.8 authorial decisions. The original archive forms and the earlier working compounds remain recoverable in version history. Long possessive chains may be unpacked with free genitive: the calendar of my past endeavours is not forced into a single unwieldy word. This improves both spoken plausibility and typesetting without reducing the approved font size.

The King's we may be a sovereign's institutional singular, distinct from lym for several individuals and from ly's earlier collective reading. Context and speaker identity establish that use; the English column and notes preserve it. Bertram's imposed marriage is grammatically an imposed act, not mutual consent. Consent, command, vow and contractual condition have separate lexical entries.

Numbers in the drama retain decimal source values even when the language's own number-writing system is duodecimal. Ten-four names fourteen; two-ten names twenty. The conventional vel­tatren (encoded veltatren) names twenty-four hours in Helena's medical deadline. These are lexical quantities, not a reinterpretation of the printed strings 14 or 24 as base-twelve values.

Dictionary archive policy
The current dramatic dictionary contains current-encoding headwords with grouped senses. Duplicate historical chart witness lists are retained in the inherited immutable Forge revisions and the ancestry bundle; they are not presented as hundreds of extra contemporary synonyms. No original input or earlier language release is overwritten. New drama entries remain marked draft until editorial review is complete.


Acts III–V: discourse, quotation and argument
Temporal and causal clauses may frame the sentence before the main clause. In continuous dialogue a subordinator may close its own clause: [clause] because, [clause] if, and [clause] though are licensed counterparts of the initial framing construction. The boundary is retained with punctuation. This is a head-final subordinate construction, not arbitrary English word scrambling. Long relative descriptions keep the referent expressed when two women, two rings, two letters or competing speakers make a gap unsafe.

An attributive state root can stand directly before its noun in a compact descriptive phrase (noble lady, fresh clothes); a heavier predication follows with the modifier construction or relative clause. Unbound genitives replace overly long compound possessors. These options are grammatical alternatives with different information weight, not random rotation through surface patterns.

Nonfinite complements can retain aspect when anteriority matters: an event nominal or perfect infinitive can distinguish having done something from intending to do it. Aspect alone does not claim an event was voluntary. Passive and causative constructions preserve the distinction between marriage commanded by a king, a promise made by a suitor, and freely offered consent.

A finite verb followed by a postposed necessity clitic scopes the obligation over the predicate. Prohibitions use ma- on the predicate before the necessity/imperative ending. A final ma after ability denies ability. When the speaker means absence of an obligation, the negated predicate is need/necessity, not the commanded act. The edited transcription records these distinctions rather than treating all English modal negatives as interchangeable.

Feigned speech in 4.1 and 4.3 is quotation, not vocabulary. Double-braced material in the editorial transcription denotes the soldiers' deliberately unintelligible performance. The readable target gives a consistent pronounceable stage sequence; the gloss explicitly says [feigned speech]. No false dictionary definitions have been invented for those syllables. The exact English-source sequences remain in the English column. Actors must not infer a hidden foreign-language translation from them.

Person and testimony
The same ring is referred to differently by a witness's claim, actual ownership and present possession. A free genitive or possessive expresses the claim in that utterance; it does not certify it. The two ring exchanges remain distinct. Diana's denials in 5.3 are intentionally incompatible on their surface. They are not normalized into a single consistent story before Helena appears.

The second-person familiar form follows downward address, intimacy and rebuke; the respectful/plural form follows formal petitions and public examination. Social rank is not the only factor. Formulaic court address is allowed to repeat, while subject expression and clause framing vary with reference and emphasis. The King's institutional we, ordinary individual I and plural we remain distinct.

Stage labels, directions and the epilogue are translated as part of the source. Proper names keep consistent adapted forms and Maxima initials. Text remains literal legacy slots: neither Unicode uppercasing nor normalization substitutes for the Thimfora identity-pair map. The transliteration column is exactly the same string in the intended Transliteration 7 font, including case.

Dictionary presentation
Regularly declared adverbs, comparatives and superlatives are listed as variants under the base headword, with their complete surface forms and separate gloss senses. This avoids counting a form like more-bright as an unrelated new root. Equal inherited headwords acquire new explicitly draft senses without discarding their old definitions or record IDs. The complete editorial dictionary export also contains component roots and every semantic key used by the transcription, including compound components that never occur alone.

Editorial status
This is a complete authored first translation in the proposed 0.8 dramatic branch, not a claim that a mature community has attested these new rules. It is designed to be read and revised: the source ledger, construction analyses, lexical derivations and commentary remain available. Automated checks establish coverage, valid symbols and layout; they do not establish literary equivalence. Uncertain readings and untransferred puns remain documented.

grammar.label: Tracking the subject of attendant actions
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
1. Tracking the subject of attendant actions
The inherited converb -’es now has an explicit same-subject interpretation within an attendant-action chain. A subject switch must be stated. New -’esta (cv.ds.) marks a background action whose subject differs from the main clause's subject. The background subject is explicit or locally unambiguous; the ending itself supplies no person, gender, or number. Thus Titania sleep:cvds, clowns enter:pr says that Titania sleeps while the clowns enter, not that the clowns sleep. In 0257 and 0511 this matters for stage directions; in 0372 one faithful man's holding his oath contrasts with the million who fail. A named subject with while remains an ordinary alternative; the new suffix is not required merely because English contains while. An infinitive complement is not an attendant action.

The annotated production order is stem + derivation/voice + converb. A finite tense and a converb are alternative clause forms here. Temporal anchoring comes from the main clause and context. A change from dreamer to visitor is never licensed by simply dropping the subject. Unit 0142 uses ordinary -’es: the aunt telling her story is also the aunt who mistakes Puck for a stool. This contrast is a useful regression example.

grammar.label: Wishes, commands, and spells
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
2. Wishes, commands, and spells
The ordinary direct imperative remains -e (imp.); an invitation or command can be refused. The inherited -’ne (opt.) expresses a wish. New -’rai (rit.juss.) presents a state as being imposed by a ritual utterance. It follows the tense/aspect form in the spell register: love:pr:juss, be:pr:juss. It is used in the love enchantments, reversal, and final household blessing. The ending expresses the speaker's performative intention, not an omniscient guarantee that a spell succeeds. A character can misapply a spell. An enchantment producing attraction is not consent.

Negation has an explicit scope. neg:imp prohibits the imperative action. neg:pr:juss imposes the absence of the specified state. A negative quantifier such as never may instead range over a positive predicate; it is not then a second negating morpheme. In Oberon's final blessing (0750), no mark is to stand in the offspring. Translating a protective spell as a positive prediction of harm would reverse the sense. The lullaby retains its repetition as an intentional refrain. Ritual repetition is distinct from a default prefix accidentally added to every sentence.

grammar.label: Reported claims and apparent identity
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
3. Reported claims and apparent identity
New -’vë (rep.) follows a finite predicate and marks information attributed to a prior speaker or report. An explicitly named source is retained when material. In 0232 Robin's identification of the sleeping man is based on his master's description; the reportative keeps that identification inside Robin's mistaken inference. It does not certify that Lysander is Demetrius. A quoted assertion is still quoted speech and need not be redundantly reportative.

New -’sëm (appr.) marks an apparent or perceived proposition: seem-to-be, appear-to-do. It is not a generic past tense and does not assert deception or falsehood. Hermia's apparent scorn in 0414 belongs to a character's perception. Awakening lovers can describe appearances without settling whether the night was a dream. Attach these particles after the finite tense/aspect form; do not stack them as decoration. This edition has no productive rule for arbitrary evidential stacking. Where attribution and appearance both matter, use a full reporting clause plus an apparent predicate.

grammar.label: Counterfactual resemblance
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
4. Counterfactual resemblance
venki (asif) introduces a comparison to an imagined situation. It differs from ordinary as (role/comparison) and from an open if condition. The comparison's predicate carries -’ve when the situation is counterfactual or imagined as unreal. Oberon's arrow might have pierced a hundred thousand hearts (0173): the narrator need not assert that it did. Titania's pregnant friend imitates a swelling ship (0162–0163): woman, belly, ship, and sails remain distinct participants. This extension gives comparisons explicit scope without turning every poetic image into a literal identity.

grammar.label: Controlled variation and information structure
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
5. Controlled variation and information structure
Keep 0.8's object–subject–verb preference, differential subject marking, and recoverable topical subjects. Topic-first, contrastive object-first, direct address, and finite predicate ellipsis have discourse reasons. The lovers often repeat another speaker's exact construction to contradict it. Hermia and Helena's matched more...more clauses (0065–0066) preserve that parallelism rather than manufacturing synonyms. The craftsmen's hesitant fragments, fairy refrains, courtly periods, and Robin's compact asides remain different registers.

Bare noun adjuncts form compact classifications; descriptive count modifiers can follow the head with ’mç. A light preposed attribute is available in established dramatic phrases, especially names, vocatives, and predicates. This does not abolish case on the phrase head. Head-internal possessors have genitive scope; the final head bears outer case. Prefer a free relation with of or a genitive when a stack obscures the relationship: queen of the fairies, rather than an indefinitely concatenated possessive. Layout never changes the font to rescue an opaque compound.

The choice of a bare noun, thing-class introduction, pronoun, or lexical synonym follows reference and register. It is not randomized. New wood, garden, craft, and theatre vocabulary reduces pressure to reuse generic thing/person/make compounds for every image. Deliberate rhetorical recurrence remains recurrence. This is a written dramatic register, not a claim that all speakers in an imagined community use the same style.

grammar.label: Quantity, collective reference, and numeral identity
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
6. Quantity, collective reference, and numeral identity
Generic one (vem) is a pronoun, not the numeral one. Numeric one uses the attested neksus; eight uses the attested krizum. The inherited ly is collective/royal we; lym identifies plural participants. Singular collective reference is not a typographical error. Dual forms are used where a pair is intended, including eyes and arms; a collective crowd is not automatically dual.

Do not reinterpret the play's hundred thousand, million, miles, or leagues as different quantities because Unta is duodecimal. Decimal source quantities retain their value; lexical quantity phrases and units are explicit. Older 0.8 authored counting forms are retained for compatibility and remain separately documented from the Unta archive. This edition clarifies one versus generic one; it does not silently recase or replace every numeral in the inherited dictionary.

grammar.label: Orthography and the four reading columns
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
7. Orthography and the four reading columns
Thimfora and Transliteration 7 receive identical legacy slots, including Maxima. A source speech split for pagination does not create a new sentence capital. Capitalization follows actual Maxima/Minima identity pairs at sentence starts and proper names; Unicode upper/lower conversion is invalid for these encodings. Speaker labels keep their own identities. A spelling that resembles an accented Latin letter is a font slot, not an instruction to normalize it.

The construction gloss is abbreviated, in target word order: nominal case, number, person/register, voice, tense/aspect, and the new clause distinctions are explicit. pr = prs.; pa = pst.; cv.ds. = different-subject converb; rit.juss. = ritual jussive; rep. = reportative; appr. = apparent proposition; irr. = irrealis; opt. = wish. The free English column preserves the supplied text. The gloss is an explanation of construction, not a second claim to reproduce Shakespeare's English rhythm.

grammar.label: Boundaries of this revision
grammar.notes: Historical/reference scope: for new dramatic composition use the consolidated 0.10 reference; earlier rules retain their original version context.
grammar.statement:
8. Boundaries of this revision
Four new productive suffixes are declared: -’esta, -’rai, -’vë, -’sëm. venki is a new comparative subordinator. There is no new iterativity suffix in the released transcription. Existing repetition, frequentative lexical meanings, and adverbs suffice. More extensive evidential combinations, dialect histories, phonological allomorphy, and metrical scansion remain open research topics; they are not asserted to have been solved by this play.

grammar.label: 1. Clause order and reference
grammar.statement:
1. Clause order and reference

Neutral transitive clauses prefer object–subject–verb. A continuing topic can precede its object; a focused object can precede the subject. Case, discourse and punctuation must keep participant roles recoverable. This permits variation with a reason, not arbitrary permutations. Lexical subjects can take nominative -läy; fronted objects and nominal predicates use accusative -get. Nominative may be absent on an established, unambiguous subject. Pronouns are ordinarily unmarked as subjects. Restore the subject after a speaker change, topic shift, competing referent or contrast. Never let a page break decide who did an action.

Titles, vocatives, headings, dictionary citation forms and answer fragments may be bare. Lists can share a predicate. Balanced proverbial or antithetical clauses may omit a recoverable copula. An unfinished sentence stays unfinished. A source-unit split used for pagination is not a new sentence.

grammar.label: 2. Nouns, modifiers, case and possession
grammar.statement:
2. Nouns, modifiers, case and possession

The thing-class prefix remains available for classification, contrast and emphatic introduction. A known lexical noun does not require it on every appearance. This is the 0.8 dramatic extension of earlier restricted omission; do not apply old prefix-required tests to new dramatic prose without their historical context.

Count plural -un and dual -et precede case. A collective or generic class need not be pluralized; mass nouns receive count marking only for portions or kinds. A light descriptive attribute may precede its head. A heavier descriptive modifier follows with ’mū, or uses an explicit relative. Qualifying stems precede heads in compounds. One head receives one outer case: nominative, accusative, dative, genitive, source, location, goal or means. Modifier/adverb conversion is a separate category.

Bound possessors precede a head with ’; nested possessors scope inward. The final head bears the outer case. Free genitive ’i or linker i replaces an opaque chain. Use each:dat of you, not you:gen:dat: the latter attaches competing cases to one head. Spatial adpositions remain available alongside ’tha (source), ’ni (location), ’ra (goal) and ’rin (means). An external agent, an instrument and a companion are different relations, even when English uses with/by for several of them.

grammar.label: 3. People and social register
grammar.statement:
3. People and social register

Keep I singular, collective/institutional we and individuated plural we distinct. A ruler’s institutional we is not evidence of several bodies. Formal/plural you and familiar singular you reflect intimacy, public formality, rebuke or rank in the scene; they are not assigned mechanically from speaker rank. He, she, animate they and inanimate it retain the inherited proposed paradigm.

Generic vem denotes a person or a human anaphor (someone, one who). Cardinal neksus denotes one counted member, including a selected person. A measured mile, one grape, one in ten, one by one and one shared cry require quantity. Nonhuman elliptical one can use the cardinal with its recoverable noun. This distinction is now applied to both plays. Do not blindly replace every English one.

grammar.label: 4. Tense, aspect and voice
grammar.statement:
4. Tense, aspect and voice

The finite pattern is root + voice/derivation + tense/aspect. Present ow, past iz and future at combine with simple ya, progressive am or perfect fu where declared in morphology.json. A perfect relates an earlier event to a reference state; it is not a stylistic synonym for past. The reduced generic ya expresses dispositions or maxims, not necessarily an event happening now. A source will may express desire or intention rather than future tense.

Passive im, causative ar, reflexive ir and reciprocal il precede the clause ending. Ordered combinations preserve scope: passive then causative means causing something to be undergone; causative then passive means undergoing a caused event. Do not sort the suffixes alphabetically or equate these constructions. A passive need not supply an agent absent from the source. Commands, imposed marriage, consent, promises and contractual conditions remain semantically distinct.

Infinitive ’en marks a complement; a perfect infinitive is licensed for anteriority, as in having amended one’s faults. It retains the inherited perf:inf spelling; it does not locate an independent present-tense event. Other finite-tense-plus-infinitive stacks are not licensed by this baseline. Event nominalization ef’ and zero conversion remain available, with the grammatical role determined by the construction.

grammar.label: 5. Attendant actions and subject tracking
grammar.statement:
5. Attendant actions and subject tracking

The converb ’es has a same-subject interpretation in an attendant-action chain. Different-subject ’esta requires an explicit or locally unambiguous background subject. Titania sleeping while the clowns enter is not the clowns sleeping as they enter. The suffix itself identifies neither person nor gender. An overt while-clause is an ordinary alternative. Both converbs follow voice and exclude an independent finite tense. An infinitive complement is not an attendant action.

These are discourse rules. The compiler checks incompatible endings; it cannot infer the correct referent from Shakespeare. The editor must record participants in the source-aligned analysis and review ambiguous pronouns.

grammar.label: 6. Mood, modality and negation
grammar.statement:
6. Mood, modality and negation

Imperative e directs an action. Optative ’ne expresses a wish, including inherited tenseless wishes. Ritual jussive ’rai follows a finite form and presents a state as imposed by a ritual utterance. It describes the speaker’s performative intention, not guaranteed success. Preserve the distinction in spells and their reversals.

Possibility/permission, ability, necessity and defeasible expectation remain distinct. A free modal precedes its scope; an unstressed bound modal can follow the finite predicate. Do not duplicate a free modal with its bound equivalent. Irrealis ’ve expresses a hypothetical/counterfactual interpretation and may follow a modal.

Negative ma before a constituent is narrow in scope. Predicate negation before a necessity ending means necessity of not acting: must not slumber. Negating need means absence of obligation: need not slumber. Final ma can deny a completed assertion or ability. Keep these scopes explicit. Lest already encodes avoidance; adding a negative can reverse it. A negative quantifier is not automatically a redundant second negation.

Thimfora has no exclamation mark. Marked expressive force uses the new clause-final enclitic **’hā** (encoded **’hÅ**, gloss **excl.**). It attaches to the final host after that host’s case, tense, mood or reportative ending; its scope is the completed utterance. Thus an emphatic statement, urgent command, intense wish and expressive ritual utterance remain different constructions: pr:excl, imp:excl, opt:excl and pr:juss:excl. It can also follow a nominal fragment or vocative without inventing a missing verb. Close with the ordinary sentence separator, not a borrowed exclamation glyph.

The enclitic marks the speaker’s heightened affect or emphatic delivery. It does not specify anger versus joy, increase factual certainty, impose a command by itself, or change negation scope. An unmarked command remains a command; an emotionally charged event does not automatically require expressive grammar. Existing authored exclamations are migrated with their original command/wish/statement distinctions; the English retains its punctuation. In new writing, choose the marked form for discourse reasons, not for every sentence. This is a 0.10 authored construction, not an archival discovery.

grammar.label: 7. Claims, appearance, subordination and comparison
grammar.statement:
7. Claims, appearance, subordination and comparison

Reportative ’vë follows a finite predicate and attributes the proposition to a report. Apparent ’sëm marks a perceived or seeming proposition; it asserts neither certainty nor necessarily deception. Keep a materially relevant reporter visible. Arbitrary stacking of these particles is not licensed; express a reporting clause plus an apparent proposition when both matter.

Use explicit content and relative boundaries where roles could be confused. A resumptive participant or overt relation can identify a relative’s role. An initial framing subordinator or a clearly punctuated clause-final subordinator is licensed for temporal, causal, conditional and concessive clauses. Open if and counterfactual asif differ. Venki introduces imagined resemblance; irrealis belongs on the imagined predicate. Ordinary role/comparison uses the inherited comparison construction.

Polar questions, interrogative families, interrupted dialogue and quoted assertions keep their inherited readings. Quoted soldiers’ feigned speech is marked as such and is not assigned fictitious dictionary meanings.

grammar.label: 8. Lexicon, variation and ambiguity
grammar.statement:
8. Lexicon, variation and ambiguity

Use the canonical semantic keys in lexicon.json. Each key has one current form, meaning, provenance and stable semantic identifier. Distinct meanings may share a headword. Explicit historical forms are readable alternatives for old editions, not fallback defaults for new work. The package resolves the old twelve competing TSV declarations once; future file ordering cannot choose a word’s meaning.

Bar as a rigid object remains zaril; bar_obstruct restores boundary+close for preventing action. Mortal now uses die+able, distinct from dead. Existing deadly serves lethal danger. All’s Well 0024 retains its ambiguous historical mortal wording under mortal_legacy: this audit does not pretend to settle that literary reading. Do not generalize this exception to new prose.

Related polysemy, nominal/verbal conversion, conventional names and contextual homophones remain. Ten unrelated homophone groups are explicitly listed for contextual review (for example bone/noise and parent/leg). They have separate semantic keys. Similar sound alone is not proof of an error; equally, dictionary grouping is not proof of shared meaning. Expand an ambiguous phrase with an existing descriptive constituent or propose a reviewed lexical distinction when a new passage requires it.

Choose variants for reference, scope and register. Courtly address, fairy refrains, hesitant craftsmen, paired rebuttals, parallel more…more constructions and a character’s deliberately wrong words may repeat. Do not optimize diversity by random synonym replacement. Frequency and repetition reports are diagnostics, not a substitute for a readable scene. Rare reportative and different-subject forms remain proposals with limited examples, not evidence of a complete dialect history.

grammar.label: 9. Quantity and the Unta evidence
grammar.statement:
9. Quantity and the Unta evidence

The directly checked names for values zero through twelve are fōlem, neksus, thātus, venik, bārum, jensis, ōdēum, pärsus, krizum, deksin, eshnä, yamen, ämēnō. Note bārum’s macron and pärsus’s diaeresis. The package preserves exact Thimfora symbol identities through the approved Roman mapping.

New composition uses those names. Earlier tatus, tren, ketren, pent, sept and dükal remain historical readings in versioned records. Declared productive compounds follow their updated components. Ordinal second, third and fourth use the corresponding cardinal plus ’t; lexical first/neks and once/veneks remain conventional inherited exceptions. Cardinal two and ordinal second are no longer one form.

Source quantities retain their mathematical value. Decimal hundred and thousand remain explicit source-culture quantities; they do not become 144 or 1728. Ten-fourteen/fifty-type conventional decimal compounds retain the declared additive or multiplicative interpretation; new source quantities should be recorded with an exact value. Written Unta 10 means twelve, while the word eshnä denotes decimal ten. Act and scene labels retain their original displayed values. This consolidation does not change page-number glyphs or the formatter. The chart’s higher numeral readings need further systematic treatment; do not extrapolate unverified spoken forms from its highest powers.

grammar.label: 10. Orthography, gloss and testing
grammar.statement:
10. Orthography, gloss and testing

Use the approved Maxima/Minima identity map at real sentence starts and proper names. Never Unicode-uppercase or normalize legacy font slots. A continuing sentence split across source units remains a continuing sentence. Thimfora and Transliteration 7 receive identical slots and case. The gloss follows target order and abbreviates grammatical roles; the English remains the supplied source, not a reverse translation of the gloss.

Canonical compiler checks cover declared vocabulary, compatible case/number/tense, clause-form exclusivity, voice order and particle placement. The minimal pairs include valid constructions and intentional invalid contrasts. Neither successful compilation nor a Forge page test proves literary equivalence. The two full ledgers preserve every source unit, explicit edits, lexical migration and paragraph starts. The old editions and their original test results remain historical evidence. New translation work begins by loading the pinned 0.10 package and branching the consolidated Forge project, then records its own additions and review decisions.

grammar.label: 1. What the chronology means
grammar.statement:
1. What the chronology means

The frozen Bible is the historical literary witness. The two plays use a later dramatic standard. Project creation dates are not fictional language dates: 0.10 was assembled before the Bible, and 0.11 reconciles that work with the subsequently developed historical witness. This is authored language history, not a claim of archaeological attestation. The awkward Biblical translation is a particular foreign-text register, not a specimen of every ancient speaker's ordinary conversation.

The Bible is never rewritten by this work. Historical forms can survive in ritual, quotation and deliberate archaism. New translations start from 0.11 and record their own versioned additions. They must not silently start from either an earlier play compiler or the frozen Biblical dictionary.

grammar.label: 2. Inherited grammar and later developments
grammar.statement:
2. Inherited grammar and later developments

The ordinary tense, aspect, voice, case and mood inventory remains conservative. There is no invented wholesale sound shift and no random replacement of suffixes. Later change is visible in wordhood, reference and register: familiar compounds can become single inflecting words; case marking becomes less obligatory for an established, recoverable topic; dialogue permits carefully licensed omission rather than repeating a full formal introduction at every turn.

The inherited thing-class prefix remains productive in explicit classification, unfamiliar referents and marked ritual diction. It is not mechanically attached to every noun in a later conversation. Preserve the actual numeral values, negation, modal strength and participant roles. A source page break cannot reset reference.

The specific lexicalizations are listed in lexical-decisions.json. For example, historical **hefak gur** becomes ordinary **hefakgur** (war), and **pom sōlum** becomes **pomsōlum** (scholar). Old spaced phrases remain available as deliberate formal constructions. These are bounded conventional words, not a rule stripping spaces from arbitrary text. Long descriptive names can remain phrases. Outer inflection belongs to the final head of such a phrase; ordinary free phrases should instead be authored with explicit constituent analyses when internal roles matter.

grammar.label: 3. Four first-person perspectives
grammar.statement:
3. Four first-person perspectives

**I(sg.)** is one speaking self; **I(pl.)** is internal plurality within a speaking identity; **we(sg.)** is a group or office construed as one acting whole; **we(pl.)** is several individuated participants. Later speech inherits all four possibilities. The plural-I construction remains marked and available; it is not compulsory for gods, magical characters, emotional conflict or actors playing a part.

The King can invoke his office with singular-we, then return to personal I. This alternation conveys a change of stance. It does not authorize changing an English personal *me* into royal *us*. The 0.11 review restores four such personal references in All's Well. Bertram's formal response on accepting military command uses office-oriented singular-we, while *my strength* remains personal; this is explicitly an interpretive decision.

Generic observations about several people, paired individuals and an audience usually use plural-we unless the passage presents one corporate agency. **ourpl/**, **ourspl** and **ourselvespl** keep possessive and reflexive number consistent. **ourone/** explicitly selects collective possession. The older **our/** remains collective for compatibility, not a catch-all English-our translation. Spell out the intended interpretation in an analysis rather than relying on the surface ambiguity of English *we*.

grammar.label: 4. Dialogue economy and its limits
grammar.statement:
4. Dialogue economy and its limits

Unmarked established subjects and recoverable same-subject continuations are ordinary later usage. A local nominative can be omitted when case or discourse still uniquely identifies the roles. An overt subject returns after a competing participant or meaningful contrast; it must never disappear merely to reduce repeated shapes.

The paired Hermia/Helena *more I hate/love, more he follows/hates me* exchange licenses first-person subject ellipsis in its first half: each speaker supplies the deictic centre of her own antiphonal turn. The second half retains **I(acc.)** and overt **he**, keeping the role reversal explicit. This is a narrow conversational development from the older overt-subject preference, not permission to erase all turn-initial pronouns. Parallel syntax is deliberately preserved because it carries the joke and emotional contrast.

The independent examples and source-linked revision ledger document this permission. Mechanical compilation does not decide whether a referent is recoverable. In particular Helen's *he desires some private speech* retains **he** after her own *I have spoken*: the subject changes there.

grammar.label: 5. Native vocabulary and editorial repairs
grammar.statement:
5. Native vocabulary and editorial repairs

Common words use native stems and transparent native derivations. Person and place names may retain adapted source sounds. Source-culture ranks, coins, measures, animals and objects retain their distinctions: translating them natively does not turn a groat into a penny or a thousand into a different quantity.

Some 0.10 forms were unjustified imitations of source words. Their replacement is an editorial correction, not evidence that the fictional language passed through an English-like phase. Native corrections developed in the historical project are adopted where applicable, and additional dramatic terms receive explicit native derivations or deliberately authored roots. The frozen Bible is not silently repaired where it still contains a problematic older form.

The **marry** key is an assent-oath, now a native emphatic assent. It is not the verb **wed**. Every inflected use mistakenly expressing marriage through the oath is repaired in the plays; passive and causative order is preserved. The native ratification **kom rē’ne**, approximately *so may it be*, replaces the sound *amen* while retaining repeated assent where the source repeats it.

grammar.label: 6. Wordplay and social voice
grammar.statement:
6. Wordplay and social voice

Quince's confused *paramour/paragon* pair receives the deliberately authored native pair **yalangz/farangz**, illicit-beloved versus admired-exemplar. Both share the love stem; the first is a conventional colloquial contraction of forbidden-love, the second a courtly good-love epithet. Flute corrects that same pair. This preserves a plausible native verbal mistake and its explanation; it does not claim to reproduce English sounds exactly or change every use of paragon into this epithet.

Bottom's pretentious address keeps an inflated native title. Correcting every comic malapropism into polished language would destroy his voice. The dolphin/dauphin and married/marred sound plays do not transfer intact; their literal claims remain and the commentary records the loss. Do not pretend a footnote recreates a spoken joke.

The Countess's *mortal* in All's Well 0024 remains a narrow, explicitly unresolved literary reading, retained as **mortal_legacy**. It is an editorial exception, not productive later vocabulary. Metre, every pun and independent literary certification remain outside the structural validation claim.

grammar.label: 7. Dictionary scopes and reproducible continuation
grammar.statement:
7. Dictionary scopes and reproducible continuation

The package distinguishes **later-standard**, **later-literary**, **historical-reference** and **editorial-exception** entries. Historical-only vocabulary remains searchable and traceable to the frozen witness; its availability is not automatic approval for ordinary later speech. Promote it consciously, recording semantic or register change and provenance. Stable semantic keys keep histories distinct from preferred spellings.

The Forge branch descends from the pinned consolidated 0.10 head. It does not clone the huge Bible ancestry or modernize its commits. The new snapshot contains dictionary records, a current grammar wiki, decisions, source-linked play tests and focused grammatical contrasts. Original source text, all 1,970 units, Maxima and the four-column reading structure remain traceable. Save/reopen, coverage, paragraph alignment and folio tests validate the edition's construction; they do not certify literary equivalence.

grammar.label: Additive clauses and recoverable continuation
grammar.statement:
Additive clauses and recoverable continuation

The inherited independent conjunction remains available, particularly for
antiphonal replies, cumulative oaths, lists, rhetorical emphasis and performance.
An additive clause can instead place **’ã** (Roman **’oi**, analysis `:add`)
after its first complete phonological host. It preserves addition: it does not
mean “therefore”, “then”, or “but”. A speaker label or punctuation is not a host.
The host keeps case, number, possession, tense and force. The clause clitic is
outside these word endings. It can mark a licensed additive answer fragment.

Unmarked juxtaposition (`:cont`, no spoken segment) is licensed for a locally
recoverable same-actor sequence, with every original argument and verb retained.
It is not random deletion of “and”, not automatic subject omission, and not
permission to merge speakers. In this edition two explicitly reviewed narrative
sequences in Oberon's speech use it. Other cases retain an audible link.

grammar.label: Relations and dependent roles
grammar.statement:
Relations and dependent roles

Inherited bound relational chains `:relpair` **’yë**, `:reltriple` **’yër**,
and `:relquad` **’yël** preserve two, three, or four analytical relation levels.
They follow the first host of the governed phrase and expand back to the same
left-edge relation stack. They are an available literary construction, not a
command to replace ordinary possessives. The two 0.11 play ledgers contain no
adjacent `of of` stacks; this edition therefore invents none to demonstrate them.
Distinct nested heads can retain ordinary genitive marking. A human-authored
scope analysis is required: shorter print alone does not validate a relation.

The dependent personal-pronoun allomorph `:dep` **’em** can distinguish an
oblique pronoun beside a free pronoun. It retains BOTH pronouns, their referents
and all number distinctions, including I(pl.) and we(sg.). It cannot attach to a
possessive chain or arbitrary noun. No such collision was found in either play.
The finite dependent-boundary clitic `:subend` **’eth** makes a clause boundary
audible where dependent and matrix predicates happen to be identical. It does
not erase either predicate. An author must establish that dependency first.

grammar.label: Dramatic repetition is evidence
grammar.statement:
Dramatic repetition is evidence

All 19 adjacent repeated-word/predicate cases found in the two prior ledgers are
retained. “No, no”, “write, write”, “pray, pray, pray”, “ever, ever”, “a truth's a
truth”, and “which is which” have semantic or dramatic jobs. The fairies' three
“And I” replies, Titania's “for her sake” parallelism, Hermia's cumulative oath,
Quince's stilted instructions, Bottom's doggerel and Robin's closing appeal keep
their deliberate patterns. Twenty explicit source-unit decisions replace only
clause linkage. There is no random synonym cycling and no global deduplication.

grammar.label: Vocabulary, identity and typography
grammar.statement:
Vocabulary, identity and typography

Six inherited bound grammatical forms are added to the versioned dictionary;
there are no new lexical roots and no changes to existing lexical forms. The
zero continuation is a construction, not a seventh dictionary word. All 0.11
scope labels, native vocabulary, literary exceptions, four first-person voices,
pronoun choices, wordplay decisions and exclamatory grammar remain in force.
Maxima follows actual sentence/speaker boundaries, never page breaks. The two
script/reading columns retain byte-identical legacy-slot text. Source English,
source-unit order, line ranges, continuation metadata and quantities are exact.

grammar.label: Validation limits
grammar.statement:
Validation limits

Both plays are complete; every source unit is checked and newly laid out with
the approved sizes, geometry, paint, leading and paragraph alignment. The delta
lists the exact changed windows and reasons. Structural checks and translator
self-review do not constitute independent literary certification or recovery of
all Shakespearean metre and wordplay.

grammar.label: Names, homonyms and construction labels
grammar.statement:
# Later dramatic Vayrshemon 0.13 — names without lookup labels

This is a targeted audit of both complete plays against the pinned 0.12 language.
The completed historical Bibles are untouched. No biblical text is recompiled.

## Printed words and dictionary identities

Bottom, Flute, Snout, Cobweb and Mote are printed without the internal “-name”
qualifier. Bear and odour lose the “-animal” and “-stage” lookup qualifiers.
Explicit resolved labels also apply inside possessive chains: Bottom’s name
must not become “bottom-name” again when used before another noun. Pronominal
possessives retain my/your/our and their existing number distinctions. This is
a construction-gloss correction; it never substitutes English into native text.

## Separate referents, including homonymous names

Diana’s altar in Midsummer belongs to Dian the goddess, not to the Widow’s
daughter in All’s Well. The two Helen allusions in Midsummer refer to Helen of
Troy, not Helen of All’s Well or Helena of Athens. Francis Flute receives his
own identity, distinct from the Saint Francis inn-sign. Equal name sounds do
not establish equal people. The two new semantic entries preserve existing
name forms; Diana’s altar uses the established native goddess-name Dian.

## Native ordinary vocabulary

Puritan, Papist, Shrove Tuesday, centaur, Bacchanal and the epithet le Grand
were wrongly excused as names. Their new forms use existing native roots,
with precise source-specific meanings retained in the dictionary. Papist keeps
the source speaker’s polemical context; it is not a neutral label imposed on
modern people. The Shrove Tuesday phrase retains that exact calendar referent.
No Unta weekday correspondence is invented. Centaur describes a creature class;
Bacchanal denotes the wine deity’s adherent, not generic drunkenness.

“Amen, amen” already has native **kom rē’ne** twice. Preserve both ratifications
and their optative force; display the construction as **so-be(opt.)** rather
than hiding it behind the foreign formula. Neither play uses a Jesus entry.
The author’s Yeshūa spelling remains the choice for future occurrences.

## Deliberate forms retained

Bottom’s Ercles, Phibbus and Thisne, and the play-within-the-play’s Limander,
Shafalus and Procrus, are source-grounded theatrical distortions. Do not silently
normalize them. Genuine names such as Mile End and the literal fairy names
retain their referents. Limbo is a named otherworld region; the Muses and Furies
are named mythic collectives in these passages. Low Dutch is a named language
with an inherited geographic form; this audit does not invent a more precise
modern dialect identity. Regional affiliation terms are retained as documented
name-derived forms, not treated as unrelated ordinary lexical loans.

All four first-person perspectives, inherited clause variation, deliberate
repetitions, source order and English are preserved. Maxima follows names and
actual sentence boundaries. The source-linked audit is not independent literary
certification or an assertion that no other translation issue can exist.

grammar.label: The Phoenix and Turtle · source decisions
grammar.statement:
00001 · "The Phoenix and Turtle"

Back-translation: Phoenix and Turtle [the dove].

Review: Title identities refer to the poem’s birds, not to a reptile or asserted historical people.

00002 · Let the bird of loudest lay On the sole Arabian tree Herald sad and trumpet be, To whose sound chaste wings obey.

Back-translation: May the bird of the loudest song, on the sole Arabian tree, be a sorrowful herald and trumpet, whose sound chaste wings obey.

Review: The heralding bird is not arbitrarily identified as the Phoenix. The sole tree and plural chaste wings remain; herald/trumpet retain the ceremonial metaphor.

00003 · But thou shrieking harbinger, Foul precurrer of the fiend, Augur of the fever's end, To this troop come thou not near.

Back-translation: But you, shrieking forecomer, foul precursor of the fiend, foreteller of fever’s end: do not come near this gathering.

Review: No unprinted species is assigned to the ominous bird. Fever’s end remains ominous and is not mistranslated as recovery. Troop is a gathering of mourners, not an army.

00004 · From this session interdict Every fowl of tyrant wing, Save the eagle, feathered king; Keep the obsequy so strict.

Back-translation: Exclude every tyrant-winged bird from this gathering except the eagle, feathered king; keep the funeral thus strict.

Review: The eagle is the stated exception, not an added prohibition. The imperative’s scope covers the assembly and exact ritual observance.

00005 · Let the priest in surplice white, That defunctive music can, Be the death-divining swan, Lest the requiem lack his right.

Back-translation: May the priest in a white surplice, skilled in death-music, be the death-foretelling swan, lest the requiem lack his due.

Review: Can is skill/knowledge, not permission. The possessive his is retained in the due/rite phrase rather than silently deciding every theological ambiguity. Native requiem is a hymn for the dead.

00006 · And thou treble-dated crow, That thy sable gender mak'st With the breath thou giv'st and tak'st, 'Mongst our mourners shalt thou go.

Back-translation: And you, three-lived crow, who make your black kind with the breath you give and take, shall go among our mourners.

Review: Treble retains the exact threefold lifetime claim; no comparison species or biological mechanism is invented. Our is plural participants in the mourning gathering. The source’s strange breath-generation assertion is retained.

00007 · Here the anthem doth commence: Love and constancy is dead, Phoenix and the turtle fled In a mutual flame from hence.

Back-translation: Here the anthem begins: love and constancy have died; Phoenix and Turtle fled from here in a mutual flame.

Review: The shared flame and death remain. No rebirth is supplied from the usual phoenix myth. The source’s unified predicate is preserved without forcing the birds into first-person pronouns.

00008 · So they loved, as love in twain Had the essence but in one, Two distincts, division none; Number there in love was slain.

Back-translation: They loved so that love in two had its essence only in one: two distinct, no division; there number was slain in love.

Review: Preserves the simultaneous distinction and unity, rather than flattening it to ordinary agreement or making two equal zero. Number is cardinal distinction, not a noble Count.

00009 · Hearts remote yet not asunder, Distance and no space was seen 'Twixt this turtle and his queen; But in them it were a wonder.

Back-translation: Two hearts remote but not apart; distance and no space were seen between this Turtle and his queen; outside their case it would be a wonder.

Review: The apparently contradictory distance/no-space pairing is kept. But in them is read as except in their exceptional case; this interpretation is explicit, not asserted uniquely certain. His queen preserves the source’s pair relation.

00010 · So between them love did shine That the turtle saw his right Flaming in the phoenix' sight; Either was the other's mine.

Back-translation: Love shone between them so that Turtle saw his own right flaming in Phoenix’s sight; each was the other’s own.

Review: Right/claim and reciprocal possession are kept. Mine is read as possessive mine, not a mining excavation; the English source remains available beside the gloss.

00011 · Property was thus appalled That the self was not the same; Single nature's double name Neither two nor one was called.

Back-translation: Property was appalled that the self was not the same; the one nature’s twofold name was called neither two nor one.

Review: Property is defining individuality with a possession resonance, not real estate. Both negated alternatives survive. The one/two paradox is deliberately not rationalized.

00012 · Reason, in itself confounded, Saw division grow together, To themselves yet either neither, Simple were so well compounded

Back-translation: Reason, confounded within itself, saw division growing together; in relation to themselves each yet neither; the uncombined were so well combined

Review: The logical paradox and initially simple constituents are retained. The sentence continues into the next stanza; a page/stanza boundary does not impose an extra Maxima.

00013 · That it cried, "How true a twain Seemeth this concordant one! Love hath reason, Reason none, If what parts can so remain,"

Back-translation: that it cried: how truly two this concordant one seems! Love has reason, Reason none, if what separates can remain thus,

Review: Reason’s exclamation is expressed by :excl, not an unsupported exclamation glyph. Lowercase lexical love is used with sentence Maxima. The conditional and Love/Reason reversal remain.

00014 · Whereupon it made this threne To the phoenix and the dove, Co-supremes and stars of love, As chorus to their tragic scene.

Back-translation: whereupon it made this mourning-song to Phoenix and Dove, equal supremes and stars of love, as a chorus to their tragic scene.

Review: Dove is the same Turtle protagonist, not a third bird. Co-supremes preserve equal standing. The shift from 13 quatrains to the five-stanza lament remains explicit in the following heading.

00015 · Threnos

Back-translation: Mourning-song.

Review: Threnos is translated as a native lament heading, not borrowed as a proper name.

00016 · Beauty, truth, and rarity, Grace in all simplicity, Here enclosed, in cinders lie.

Back-translation: Beauty, truth, rarity, grace in all simplicity lie here enclosed in burnt remains.

Review: All five abstract qualities and the burned remains are retained. No claim of physical resurrection is inserted.

00017 · Death is now the phoenix' nest, And the turtle's loyal breast To eternity doth rest,

Back-translation: Death is now Phoenix’s nest, and Turtle’s loyal breast rests eternally,

Review: The second-position additive preserves the coordinated second clause without another opening conjunction. The eternal rest continues into the leaving-no-posterity clause.

00018 · Leaving no posterity; 'Twas not their infirmity, It was married chastity.

Back-translation: leaving no posterity; it was not their infirmity, it was married chastity.

Review: Infertility is expressly denied; the source’s married chastity is retained rather than explained away. No descendants is not no reputation.

00019 · Truth may seem, but cannot be; Beauty brag, but 'tis not she; Truth and beauty buried be.

Back-translation: Truth may seem but cannot be; beauty may boast, but it is not she; truth and beauty are buried.

Review: The contrast between appearance and being, and the feminine Beauty reference, survive. The first modal is possibility; cannot remains inability, not a prohibition. The omitted modal in Beauty brag is recovered from the parallel may-clause, a licensed ellipsis rather than a new tense.

00020 · To this urn let those repair That are either true or fair; For these dead birds sigh a prayer.

Back-translation: Let those who are true or fair come to this ashes-vessel; sigh a prayer for these dead birds.

Review: Repair means come, not mend. Either true or fair is preserved as an inclusive invitation. The prayer is for the dead pair, with no added doctrine or rebirth.

00021 · William Shakespeare

Back-translation: William Shakespeare.

Review: The supplied author attribution is retained as permitted approximated personal-name sounds.

Self-command, firmness and measured disposition renounced by Antony’s heart in Philo’s accusation. Not bodily temperature; the martial metal-temper resonance is documented separately.

Excrement enriching the common earth in Antony’s dungy-earth image; no inherited sacrificial disposal rule or Biblical participants.
A commissioned representative or envoy, the messengers Cleopatra urges Antony to hear. No inherited deceptive-visit claim is imported.
The penalty threatened rhetorically by Antony if the world denies the lovers’ peerlessness; nominal penalty, without an added particular punishment.
An untrue utterance, Cleopatra’s teasing judgment of Antony’s extravagant assertion; nominal false, not an independently established narrator verdict.
Demonstrate that a report is true, source approves the common liar in 1.1. Does not mean moral approval of the liar or a new binding legal agreement.
Ordered or disposed in ranks, the empire imagined as an encompassing arch. The exact architectural geography is not supplied.
Personified Love invoked with her soft hours in Antony’s speech. Native love form with Maxima; no forced replacement by the masculine Cupid or an unprinted proper name Venus.
Covered in armour plates, the visual comparison to Mars in Philo’s opening speech.
A clasp joining or fastening a bodily strap, the buckles on Antony’s breast. Distinct from a buckler shield; no particular metal or mechanism is imposed.
A hand-held implement for moving air, beside bellows in the paradoxical cooling of lust. The following stage direction uses the related action verb fan.
Legal process as a summons or authoritative demand, Cleopatra’s ironic comparison of Fulvia’s and Caesar’s claims; not a workflow or an invented lawsuit.
One who renders homage, Antony’s blush personified as Caesar’s subject. The blood, not an added person, bears the metaphorical role.
Having no equal, the lovers’ claimed supremacy. Not literally having no companions or noble peers.
Make a person appear fitting or beautiful: everything becomes Cleopatra. Distinct from transform into or acquire a new state.

Philo’s derogatory Egyptian-woman designation, source gypsy. Name-affiliated native woman compound; the English Egyptian/gypsy association and its alienating slur register are recorded, not silently presented as neutral narrator fact or a new Romani character.

Move someone to anger: Enobarbus imagines Caesar provoking Antony. No Egyptian messenger or other historical participant is imported from the inherited root occasion.
Caesar’s state as his welfare or political position, threatened by plotting; not a modern welfare benefit or simply the geographic state.
Bring estranged people into agreement, source atone in Maecenas’s mediation. Distinct from ritual expiation; no sacrificial doctrine or unprinted agent is introduced.
Fabricate or piece together an excuse or quarrel, preserving the patchwork metaphor in the leaders’ exchange. Not a literal repair to their clothing.

A small glowing remnant that can rekindle fire; native fire-seed, used for the quarrel Lepidus asks Enobarbus not to stir. No literal botanical seed is asserted.
Keeping private bitter anger, source stomaching. This is resentment rather than the digestive organ or swallowing food.
The snaffle bridle mouthpiece in Antony’s comparison of ruling a third of the world and controlling a wife. Native bridle-bar; no dimensions or exact mechanical joint are invented.
A binding provision or term within an oath, cited in Caesar’s accusation. Not a newspaper article, object, or extra oath.

Cleopatra’s magnificent, showy presence as Maecenas reports it; no newly won battle is invented.
A hollow breath-played musical pipe setting the oars’ rhythm. Distinct from Francis Flute in Midsummer; no modern instrument design is imposed.

Bear a crop in Agrippa’s sexual farming metaphor for Cleopatra’s pregnancy by Julius Caesar; not reap or cut away an already-grown crop. No unprinted child name is added.
A broad boat carrying Cleopatra and her ceremonial display. Native wide-boat; no precise hull size, draught or modern engine is invented.

Imbue with a pleasing scent, the barge’s perfumed sails. Native scent converted to an action; no formula, ingredient or Biblical ritual is imported.
The steering apparatus or station of Cleopatra’s barge, native ship-turn. Distinct from a warrior’s helmet; no modern wheel or particular rudder arrangement is asserted.
Direct a vessel’s course, native ship-turn used as an action. The attendant steers; no Acts voyage or shipwreck is imported.

The bird in Antony’s comparison of fighting birds. Reuses the corrected native bird-kind term, without importing manna, wilderness events, or the verb shrink in fear.
An angled measuring square used figuratively for correct conduct, paired with the measuring rule. Not a quarrel, a plaza, an arithmetic power, or an inserted numerical angle.
A measuring rule or line, figuratively the straight standard governing Antony’s promised conduct. Not sovereignty or a political ruler.
The personal guardian spirit called daemon and angel by the soothsayer. Neither an evil demon nor an imported Biblical messenger; the supernatural claim belongs to the speaker.
Relative chances in a contest or wager, without an exact ratio unless the source supplies one. Native chance-measure; distinct from strangeness or personal disagreement.
A token drawn to decide by chance. Distinct from a landed allotment, the personal name Lot, and an unspecified large amount.

senses.definition: Adult male domestic fowl, the fighting cock in Antony’s comparison. A deliberate lexical counterpart to native hen kekla; the ending is not a productive sex-changing suffix.
The curved hook piercing fish jaws in Cleopatra’s fishing fantasy. Native fish-hook; no Biblical judgment, geometric angle or foreign hook loan is imported.
One of the named mythic Furies, imagined with snakes around her head. Distinct from ordinary anger; the individual belongs to the named collective, not a new woman surnamed Fury.
A reservoir or water-holding pit in Cleopatra’s wish that half Egypt be flooded. Native water-store-pit, without importing a siege or drinking-water claim.
A scale on a serpent’s body, extending the existing native bodily-scale category from aquatic creatures. Not weighing scales, stairs or a musical scale.

The source game of balls struck with rods, here the table game Cleopatra requests. Native ball-rod lexicalized as a game; retain the source anachronism without inventing modern pool rules or silently replacing it with an ancient game.
A fish’s projecting swimming organ, fish-wing by analogy. No claim that it flies or a distinct fish species is supplied.
Wet slippery coating on a surface, here fish jaws. Distinct from river mud and the historical earth-pitch sense of slime.
Commit a stake to the outcome of a contest, native chance-give. No monetary amount, equal stake or new rule is implied.
Ornament or dress for the head, Cleopatra’s tires placed on Antony. Not fatigue, a vehicle tyre or a specified crown.
The keeper bringing a prisoner out, used for the phrase But yet. Native prison-guard; not a host offering lodgings.
A wrongdoer, here the monstrous prisoner in Cleopatra’s metaphor for unwelcome news. No particular offense is invented.
Able to transmit illness, the pestilence Cleopatra wishes on the messenger. Native sickness-give; records the curse without an editorial claim that illness was transmitted.
Thin drawn metallic strand in Cleopatra’s threat. Native metal-thread; no electrical or later industrial apparatus is introduced.
An administratively ruled territory that Cleopatra offers as a reward. Native rule-land, no fabricated area or map boundary.
A destructive lightning stroke in Cleopatra’s claim that even innocents may be hit. Native lightning-strike, not a crossbow bolt or merely the sound of thunder.

Touch or kiss with the lips, the kings who lipped Cleopatra’s hand. Explicit nominal-to-verbal use, not an anatomical noun mistaken for a finite action.
Proclaim or announce loudly through the trumpet metaphor. Does not add an actual instrument to the messenger’s entrance.
Shower down as hail, the promised rich pearls falling on the messenger. Not a salutation, an invented weather event or an exchange of pearls for ice.

A useful service or purpose, native turn extended to the good-turn / turn-in-bed exchange. The lexical bridge carries the sexual joke without asserting that ordinary physical rotation always means marriage.
Benefit or compensate the messenger with an additional gift, source boot. Distinct from footwear and from the kicking threat in the earlier speech.
Heat while immersed in liquid, Cleopatra’s cruel imagined brine punishment. A native soak-heat action, not a claim of a performed event or a technical preparation procedure.
A person held as security in the reciprocal prebattle exchange. Native pledge-held-person, without inferring ransom, age, consent or a Biblical setting.
The Roman council-ruler designation Pompey applies to the three rulers of the world. Reuses native council-elder vocabulary without importing the Psalm’s Egyptian court or a modern constitution.
Pompey’s rowing vessel, the site of the proposed feast. Native ship-oar category; no new crew count, deck plan or ancient ship model is invented.
The negotiated political compact to be written and sealed among the rulers. Distinct from writing a literary composition or an unmentioned marriage agreement.
Counts or visible tallies left by personified Fortune on Pompey’s face. Native accounting sense, not the noble title count and not a newly invented count of scars.
A person acting as the gods’ principal business agent in Pompey’s address to the rulers. Native god-worker, preserving factors as representatives rather than arithmetic factors.
A gathered force of ships, here Pompey’s war fleet. Native ship-gather, no ship count supplied.
Preparation of food as a practiced skill, the Egyptian cookery whose reputation Pompey praises with an erotic insinuation. Not a cookbook or inserted recipe.
A padded bedding support in which the queen is reportedly carried. Native bed-cushion; preserve the supplied mattress rather than substituting a carpet from another telling.

senses.definition: The named man who carried the queen in the reported episode. The source’s unfinished sentence is completed by Enobarbus; no added personal history is supplied.
Exceed in the number of forces, Antony’s threat about land strength. No unstated ratio is supplied. Related reckoning imagery is preserved in Pompey’s counting-cheat reply.
Cheat someone out of property by reckoning, Pompey’s retort about his father’s house. The shared native reckon component echoes outcount_force without asserting more houses than the source supplies.
Frank and unadorned speech, which Pompey allows Enobarbus. Not a flat landscape or a technical vow of honesty.
The alliance or joining of Caesar and Antony through the marriage. Not a labour organization or a claim that their friendship has already become permanent.
Make a prediction about an alliance’s future, an action distinct from divine as the adjective belonging to a god. The forecast remains Enobarbus’s judgment.
Conversation in its manner-of-living sense, Octavia’s holy, cold and still disposition. Not merely how she talks in a conversation.
The explicitly printed Marcus form before Antonius. Same personal name and referent as Mark Antony, with the source variant visible in the gloss; not a new character.
A drinking salute to another’s health offered by Menas. Native health-drink, distinct from literal physical wellness or a medical treatment.
