lexicon.label: marcellus_octavia_husband

senses.definition: Marcellus, Octavia’s former husband named with Caius. Distinct from Hamlet’s guard despite the identical source surname; no internal suffix appears in the reading name.
Practical judgment and self-command, personified as at war with Lepidus after drinking. Native forethought sense without importing a Biblical teacher or moral injunction.
The Egyptian tapering monument in the Nile measurement discussion. Pyramises is a historical source variant, not evidence that Lepidus invents a wrong word; the native noun remains the same.
An earnest appeal, Lepidus’s request that the others stop provoking one another. Nominal use of the native entreat root, not an already granted command.
Irritate or needle another person through temper in the banquet servants’ exchange. Keeps the bodily pinch metaphor without adding physical violence to the reported disagreement.
Bring ruin upon or disfigure a face in the missing-eyes conceit. Explicit verbal use of native disaster; the source’s astrological overtone remains in the source-linked review.
An acting part of the body in Antony’s deliberately uninformative crocodile description. Not a musical instrument, organization or exclusively generative organ.

Constituents or life-forces in Antony’s natural-philosophy joke about an animal’s life. Native world-part does not decide between a material or vital-force reading, assert a modern chemical element, or import an apocalypse.
An opposing assertion, which Lepidus claims he has not heard about the pyramids. Native against-say used nominally; no religious disobedience imported.

The charitable-drink expression in the servants’ joke. Retains its literal native components while the source review records possible dregs given in charity or drink for reconciliation; neither reading is silently made certain.
A broad-headed pole weapon, native broad-spear, contrasted with a useless reed. Distinct from a political adherent; no exact dimensions or fighting instructions are introduced.
The ceremonial instrumental entrance signal. Native trumpet-signal, distinct from an ordinary conversation signal; no modern musical score or extra performers supplied.
A graduated mark for comparing the river’s level, the scales in the pyramid. Not a fish scale or a weighing pan; the source supplies no measured flood quantity.
One who sows grain into the receding Nile’s mud. Native sow-agent, not an inserted landowner or a trader selling seeds.
The large river reptile named in the Egyptian drinking conversation. Native river-lizard is a lexicalized creature name, not a claim about modern taxonomy or a respelling of the English/Greek word.

Pass beyond the present embodied condition, Antony’s pompous circumlocution for what occurs when the animal’s elements leave. Native beyond-go preserves the evasive joke without imposing a specific destination or doctrine of rebirth.

A person labelled through the native philosophical-school term in Antony’s joke: possibly a pleasure-seeker hard to satisfy, possibly a doubter of the proposed transmigration. Both readings remain in the review. This later literary sense does not assert the school’s doctrine as a narrator fact or import the Acts audience.
Unstable sand that allows sinking, the image Antony uses for Lepidus’s drinking hazard. No literal sand on the galley and no Acts voyage or modern mechanism is asserted.
The ship’s mooring cable which Menas proposes cutting. Native ship-cord, no modern electrical cable, exact material or mooring arrangement is added.
The Roman divine name Jove in Menas’s earthly-sovereignty comparison. Same figure as Jupiter; explicit case-correct name display, not an ordinary borrowed word for a god.
Adorn the hair or head with a wreath-like crown in the drinking song. Native crown made verbal; not payment with a coin or an unstated coronation as ruler.
Abstain from food or drink, Caesar’s comparison of four days without any against excess in one day. Explicit verbal use of native not-eat, without speed or an added religious observance.
A wine-holding vat in the song’s wish to drown cares. Native wine-container, no Biblical winepress judgment or fixed capacity is imported.
Supply someone with drink, the repeated imperative in the song. Native cup made verbal; the repetition is intentional and must stay identical.
The holding or recurring sung response assigned to all the men after the boy’s verse. Not a bodily grip, holding office or a new cast member named Chorus.
Drunkenness as an alteration of appearance or conduct in Caesar’s complaint. Keeps the disguise metaphor without inventing costumes at the feast.
A revel dance honoring the wine god, source bacchanals. Native wine-dance, distinct from the worshipper noun in the Thracian comparison and without an ordinary borrowed ritual name.
The private room aboard the vessel to which Menas invites Enobarbus. Native ship-room; no extra cabin plan or land cottage supplied.

Revelry with a turning or reeling image in the wheels/reels exchange. Native turn-revel keeps the festive motion link, though it does not recreate the English rhyme and does not specify a named later dance.

A trained writer in Enobarbus’s list of people and expressive powers. Native write-person, without importing the separate religious-law role.

A sign or figure in the list paired with thinking, speaking and reckoning. The native sign category permits numerical notation and expressive figures without inserting particular digits or treating every figure as a measurable quantity.
Proven worth or character on which Caesar offers his bond for Octavia. Not her approval of a plan and not a new examination she is ordered to pass.
Exacting and difficult to satisfy when looking for cause of distrust. Distinct from simple inquisitiveness or a fabricated investigation already completed.

The forces of nature or atmosphere wished kindly to Octavia during travel. Keeps the old elemental category without asserting modern chemical substances or the crocodile’s life-forces as identical senses.

The historical green-sickness label in the teasing report of Lepidus after the feast. Native green-illness preserves the pallor and lovesick-young-woman insinuation, without diagnosing him or substituting a modern medical condition.
A singer of poetry in the list of those unable to express Lepidus’s love. Native verse-sing-agent, distinct from the following general composer noun poet.
Number as composing or measuring verse in the rhetorical list. Native verse-measure, distinct from numerically counting the love; the parallel cast remains reckon.
The wing-covering reading of shards in the beetle metaphor. Native wing-shell; the alternative dung-patch reading is recorded as an unresolved source ambiguity, not silently declared impossible.
A building binder or mortar in the marriage-as-fortress image. Native lime-bind is a lexicalized material category, not a modern cement recipe or a new physical building project.
Fine soft bird down, the feather poised on the tide. Native soft-feather distinguishes the material from downward direction.
Watery discharge, especially of the eyes, in Enobarbus’s dismissive explanation of Antony’s tears. Native eye-flow here, not an independently diagnosed illness or simple rheumatic joint pain.
Grapple by bodily holds, Antony’s loving wrestling embrace of Caesar. Native hold-fight preserves the martial affection metaphor without adding an actual hostile contest.
Doubt in another person’s promised conduct, Antony’s response to Caesar’s warning. Native doubt used as an interpersonal noun; not a numerical uncertainty estimate or a proven accusation of betrayal.

Herod of Jewry in Alexas’s boast about Cleopatra’s fearfulness and her ensuing head-taking threat. Retains the source’s theatrical Herod identity and the already permitted personal form; does not force the play’s chronology into a different Biblical king or assign a numbered dynasty.
Standing posture or bearing contrasted with motion in the messenger’s unflattering description of Octavia. Nominal conversion of native stand, not a journey station or social office.
A gentle, unshrill manner of voice in the description of Octavia. Retains the native low image without asserting a measured low pitch, social inferiority, or a bodily height.

A raised platform supporting the golden chairs in Alexandria. Native high-floor, the spatial sense of tribunal here rather than an entire court of law.
The public area for performances or exercise in Caesar’s account. Native show-ground, without imposing a particular amphitheatre plan.
A stopping point or successive stage on Octavia’s journey, not a theatrical platform or her standing posture.

The projecting land at Actium from which Antony proposes a sea attack. Native land-head; no new coordinates or an asserted cliff height.

The disputed matter at stake, the question in Enobarbus’s mered question. Not an interrogative utterance. The exact restrictive force of mered is noted as uncertain in the source review.
Sheltering protection, the shroud Caesar’s envoy offers Cleopatra. Native keep-safe used as an action noun; not the burial cloth sense.
Competence in military command, native command-craft. Enobarbus contrasts this with Antony’s desire; not simply possession of a captain’s rank.
A territory under sovereign rule, offered in Antony’s bitter imagined reward for his own head. Native rule-land; distinct from principal sums or heavenly powers.

Display equipment or adornment in Antony’s challenge to strip off Caesar’s caparisons. Native show-clothing preserves the figurative trappings of power rather than silently following another edition’s comparisons reading.
A sword combatant, the sworder in Enobarbus’s sarcastic arena image. Native sword-fight-agent; no invented personal gladiator name.
Lord or master of land in the envoy’s universal-landlord claim for Caesar. Native land-lord retains the property metaphor without asserting modern tenancy law or worldwide historical sovereignty.
Admit water through an unsound vessel, Antony’s leaking-ship image in Enobarbus’s aside. Native water-enter used of the vessel, not a modern disclosure of secret information.
Representation through an appointed person, Cleopatra’s in-deputation greeting to Caesar. Native stand-for used nominally; no new office or physical kiss is asserted by the word alone.
Give pleasure or satisfaction to a person, the envoy’s claim about Caesar’s response. Explicit transitive verbal use of native delight, distinct from a courteous please request particle.
Defiling dirt into which Antony imagines judgment dropped; physical filth with moral metaphor, not a new medical claim.
A dish holding food in Antony’s insulting leftovers comparison; not military armour.
The fastening laces of clothing, source points tied by Caesar’s attendant; no number or pointing gesture.
Basan/Bashan in Antony’s named hill-and-cattle allusion. The same place-name, without turning a reference into Biblical-register dialogue.
Estridge in the dove comparison, read as a large predatory hawk. The source category is retained without an asserted modern species; the alternative ostrich reading is recorded in translation review.
A dependent at another’s table, used contemptuously by Antony of Cleopatra’s supposed object of attention.
The leniency Thidias asked under punishment; not the verb to favour or an already granted pardon.
Native predatory-bird compound, the bird used as an insult to Thidias; not a borrowed name or a flying toy.
The children’s scramble for thrown prizes in Antony’s comparison of eager kings; a game, not general disorder.
A ruler subordinate through tribute, not a river branch or an ordinary taxpayer.
Make a plaintive begging sound, in Antony’s imagined humiliation of the envoy.
A person who changes allegiance or intention; Antony’s accusation, not an author verdict.
Close eyelids by stitching in the falconry image; not authenticate with a seal.
Walk in ostentatious pride, the movement toward ruin in Antony’s accusation.
A rope loop around the condemned neck in the hanging comparison.
The executor of a hanging, not a person who merely hangs clothes.
The deep chasm in the imagined fall of guiding stars into hell.
A bodily mark of whipping, source stripes; not patterned clothing.
Strike with a bird’s beak; distinct from peck as a source dry measure.
An anniversary of birth observed in the present; does not assert a newborn speaker.

A rich red precious stone in the comparison with Phoebus’s chariot. Retains the source jewel category without asserting an exact modern mineral; not a skin lesion.
The small marching drum whose rattling sound mingles with the trumpets; native drum term, with the supplied subtype retained in the gloss.
Resistance to breaking or yielding, the flinty hardness of Enobarbus’s fault in his self-accusation. Abstract nominal use, not a named material.
A written record in which the world may class Enobarbus; the action record used nominally, not a new bureaucratic office.
The hacked defensive targets carried in the victory march. Native protection term as a concrete shield; distinct from target as the intended object of a shot.
The court of guard where the watch returns and carries Enobarbus. Native watch-chamber; not a royal court or a judicial hearing.
A success scored in a contest, Antony’s goal-for-goal comparison with youth. Native tally sense; not an explicit quantity of twenty or a modern sporting rule.
The nesting bird in Cleopatra’s sails, distinct from the verb take into the mouth. The omen remains the characters’ report, with no imposed modern species.
Octavia’s prepared nails in Antony’s threatened humiliation of Cleopatra; bodily nails, not fastening spikes.
The enclosure of the heart, Antony’s body as its continent. Not a geographical continent or a chastity adjective.
A winning card in Antony’s rigged-card metaphor, carrying the source triumph/victory overlap. The established native triumph word takes a contextual card sense; no English trump loan.
Antony’s affectionate my knave to Eros during the cloud comparison, not an accusation of roguery.
A marked playing leaf in the metaphor of secretly arranged cards; not a greeting card or a written letter.
Secretly arrange cards to cheat, Antony’s accusation that Cleopatra and Caesar packed cards. Native secret-arrange, not packing luggage.
The fastening-and-release trick game invoked by Antony; a native knot-trick name preserves the binding/release deception rather than mere inconsistency.

The source’s hostile Gypsy label in Antony’s Egyptian pun: an Egypt-associated wanderer in his stereotype. This native place-and-wandering formation preserves the dramatic pun without asserting that actual Romani people come from Egypt or borrowing the English ordinary label.
Ordinary people in Antony’s sneering plebeians address, not a named ethnicity or newly specified political faction.
A cleft or branching mountaintop in the changing cloud shapes; no utensil or invented measured height.

Cast down in spirit while still courageous, Scarus’s description of Antony; a contextual use of native sorrow without a medical diagnosis.
Call or summon by a sign; Cleopatra’s eye beckoning armies, not necessarily a spoken order.
The body garment in the Nessus allusion, a tunic or shirt rather than a modern buttoned design. Native body-garment.
The heavy striking weapon of Hercules; wooden striker, distinct from a social club.
Rip or tear apart, the soul/body parting and wrenching groan. Kept distinct from the noun for a tear shed by the eye.
A pointed missile weapon, the Parthian darts which failed to kill Antony; not a modern sport or an assumed arrow mechanism.
The moving cloud mass which erases its own horse-shaped outline. Rack is not a torture apparatus in this image.
Bring to completion by sealing, Antony’s finalizing metaphor. Explicit verbal use of native seal rather than an ordinary foreign loan.
Overwhelming dread in the anticipated pursuit of humiliation; no supernatural apparition is asserted.
Erase a visible outline, dislimn in the changing-cloud comparison. Does not imply destroying a living horse.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal or place name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal or place name.
lexicon.label: diomed_attendant_variant

senses.definition: The shortened address Diomed used for Cleopatra’s messenger Diomedes. Same referent as diomedes_attendant; source name variation is retained.
Distinction earned by courage or magnanimity, not inherited rank alone. Antony judges the servant Eros and his queen to have surpassed him in this quality.

An active preparation taken for its bodily effect. Cleopatra means drugs capable of causing death alongside knives and serpents; this later contextual extension of the native medicinal-preparation word does not imply that the preparation is healing or harmless.
Adorn a display as a conspicuous fastening jewel. Cleopatra refuses to be the brooch on Caesar’s imperial triumph; not a claim that she is literally pierced by a pin.

Weight with a grief sense in Cleopatra’s lifting speech. Her company’s strength has become heaviness: the native weight-family word deliberately carries both physical burden and sorrow in this passage.
A wanton woman used as Cleopatra’s insult to personified Fortune. This source huswife is not a neutral housewife or an assertion about domestic employment.
Firm determination on which Cleopatra relies with her own hands; nominal use of native resolve, not a resolution passed by an assembly.

The soldier’s elevated pole or central point of reference, the image of Antony falling. Preserve the pole image and military rallying force without claiming the disputed image can only mean the North Star or a particular festival pole.
The preeminence or distinguishing advantage Cleopatra says is gone when Antony dies. Qualitative odds, not numerical betting odds or a stated ratio.
Draw milk from an animal, the ordinary labour in Cleopatra’s comparison with a lowly maid. Verbal extension of the native substance word; not extracting money or feeding milk to a child.
An enclosure for pigs, Cleopatra’s contemptuous comparison for the world without Antony. Native animal-plus-enclosure compound, not a foreign ordinary loan.
An ordinary household task, the meanest chares in Cleopatra’s speech; no invented list of duties.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal or place name.
lexicon.label: proculeius_caesar_agent

senses.definition: Caesar’s agent whom dying Antony recommends Cleopatra trust. His identity is not merged with another Roman officer or given an internal suffix in the printed name.

Admirable in courage or magnanimity rather than only hereditary rank. The native rank word gains an explicitly recorded moral sense in Cleopatra’s noblest-of-men lament and her proposed noble conduct; not a random substitute for good.
The loud report of a great thing breaking in Caesar’s reaction to Antony’s death. A contextual audible crash, distinct from a narrow physical chink.
Open a diseased swelling by piercing to release its contents, Caesar’s bodily metaphor for destroying Antony. Native pierce, not a claim to be wielding the long military lance.
The human nature or human frame steered by a spirit in Agrippa’s praise. Nominal use of native human; distinct from benevolence alone or a count of all human beings.
A fault or blemish of character weighed against Antony’s honours. Native fault, not the verb infect another person.
Supreme or overpowering in quality, Caesar’s tears likened to the blood of hearts. A recorded figurative extension of native sovereign; not an assertion that the tears are people who rule.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal or place name.
lexicon.label: gallus_caesar_officer

senses.definition: The officer sent with Proculeius to Cleopatra. Distinct named participant; the source does not authorize identifying him with a particular poet or supplying a biography.
Cleopatra’s condition of being emptied and abandoned after Antony’s death. Nominal extension of native desolate, not a newly depopulated geographic territory.
Earth or soil named contemptuously as dung, sustaining beggar and Caesar alike in Cleopatra’s death meditation. Records the source polysemy without asserting that either literally eats excrement.
Benevolent disposition expressed in gracious treatment, Proculeius’s assurance about Caesar. Native favour extended to kindness; not native kind meaning species.
Willing compliance or submission, the dependency Proculeius asks to report. Nominal use of native submit, not a dependent territory or a medical addiction.
A distressed condition, Cleopatra’s plight that Proculeius says its author pities. Native condition in an explicitly adverse context.

A structure for hanging or displaying a body; Cleopatra imagines the pyramids serving as it. Extends native hang-wood to the function, without claiming pyramids are wooden or prescribing an execution mechanism.
The supreme Antony of Cleopatra’s dream, expanded from her actual commander to the imagined world-striding ruler. No claim that the historical Antony held a later sole imperial office.
Form the crest or crowning summit of something, Antony’s raised arm above the world. Verbal extension of native crown; not the crown coin.
The elemental medium in which a being lives, water in the dolphin comparison. Contextual matter/substance, not a modern chemical element or an unspecified habitat.
Judge an imitation inadequate or worthless, the imagined Antony putting fancy’s shadows to shame. Extends native adverse judgment without imposing criminal punishment.
Another person’s grief reflected into the hearer’s heart, Dolabella’s sympathetic rebound. Figurative extension of a returning echo, not a literal sound or physical collision.
A silver coin, the plate falling from Antony’s pocket in Cleopatra’s extravagant comparison. No exact denomination, weight, or number is specified.
Stand with legs spread on either side of something, the ocean in Cleopatra’s cosmic image of Antony. No crossing journey or measured distance is asserted.
Magnanimous character expressed in conduct, the nobleness Proculeius claims Caesar can display. Explicit native abstract derivation rather than hereditary title alone.
A ditch in the ground imagined as Cleopatra’s gentler grave. Reuses the native ground-cut noun; no new depth, location within Egypt, or digging action is added.
The bodily back in Cleopatra’s dolphin simile. Reuses the dorsal-body sense, distinct from the adverb back; no source or internal lookup label prints.

A weakness of character or conduct, Cleopatra’s conventionally gendered confession before Caesar. Native weakness; the speaker’s assertion about her sex is not adopted as a linguistic fact about women.
Join or close by stitching; Seleucus would sew his lips shut rather than lie at his peril. The source seeling/falconry resonance is noted in the verse review, without replacing lips with eyelids.
Failure to return gratitude, Cleopatra’s charge against Seleucus. Nominal use of the inherited native ungrateful form.

Valuable metal household ware in Cleopatra’s inventory beside money and jewels, distinct from the silver coins in the preceding cosmic-pocket simile. Native metal-vessel does not invent an exact material, itemized vessel shapes, or amount.
A painted heraldic shield or trophy displayed as a sign of conquest, Cleopatra’s image for conquered people. Native painted-shield; not her family name or a military head count.
The keeper accountable for Cleopatra’s valuables, Seleucus’s stated office. Native treasure-keeper, not a borrowed bureaucratic title.

lexicon.label: livia_caesar_wife

senses.definition: Livia, named with Octavia as a recipient whose intervention Cleopatra seeks with Caesar. Distinct named woman; not Livy the historian and not given an invented family-name suffix.
Extraordinarily or to an exceptional degree, Cleopatra’s rarely base insult. Contextual degree rather than how seldom the man behaves badly.
A body-front protective covering worn by the workmen Cleopatra imagines. Reuses the native apron noun without retaining the Genesis leaf material.
The countryman’s woven carrying basket; no added material, size, or hidden compartment.
The venomous snake called asp or aspic in the supplied play. Native inherited creature category, without identification as an exact modern species or a medical assertion about its bite.
The workman’s striking implement among apron and measuring rule. Instrumental noun, not the act of hammering or a weapon newly used onstage.
Greasy fatty matter on the imagined workmen’s aprons. Material sense of native fat; does not invent its cooking or industrial source.
The rustic bringer of figs and the basket, the Countryman speaker in the supplied text. Not merely a compatriot or a named individual.
Make an error. The countryman’s falliable claim deliberately uses positive capability to err where infallibility is intended; do not silently negate it.
Prepared food or a dish to be eaten, the countryman’s woman-as-food joke. Reuses the native food noun, not a newly specified plate shape.
A moist viscous residue the guard attributes to the asp on fig leaves and cave surfaces. Extended from native wet mud; the attribution remains a character’s observation, not zoological certification.
Attractive grace imagined as Cleopatra’s trapping net. Nominal attractive quality, distinct from divine favour or legal pardon.
Put a crown back into its proper arrangement, Charmian’s final task. Native restoring-to-order, not cutting or trimming material off the diadem.
The Roman officer attending a magistrate with rods and coercive authority, whom Cleopatra fears as a rude captor. Native rod-guard; no number of rods or officers is inserted.
A maker of rhyming verses, insulted by Cleopatra as scald. Native rhyme-maker; the contempt remains an explicit modifier, not an inherent judgment on all poets.
The ultimate judgment day in Cleopatra’s theatrical promise of leisure. Native judgment-day, without importing a date, numeral, or modernization of the frozen Bible.
The royal dress and insignia Iras brings in the local stage direction. No individual sceptre or other object is added where the source only says regalia.
A wandering celestial body in the source’s astrological classification, which includes the moon. Native wandering-star, not a modern scientific recategorization.
The day immediately before today in the countryman’s remembered report; no inherited Biblical event is imported.
Living bodily warmth at Cleopatra’s lips in her farewell. Nominal use of native warm, not high heat or a new fever.
Bodily swelling mentioned in the guards’ and Caesar’s observations. Nominal extension of expand; their inference about poison remains a character claim.
Death’s blow compared with a lover’s pinch. Nominal striking, distinct from the inherited verb stroke meaning caress.
An infant at a nursing breast, Cleopatra’s metaphor for the asp. The metaphor does not add an actual child to the stage.
A trace attributed to the asp by the guard, the source trail; native trace/scent extended to visible residue without identifying an actual modern species.
Engage a rider or other worker by payment; native service-pay, without the inherited earlier transaction or participants.
A handed-down social practice in the brothers’ inheritance argument; not automatically a religious command or a condemned teaching.
The fruit garden in Oliver’s household where Orlando answers him; no particular trees or plan are supplied.
The source crown coin in Orlando’s inheritance, not a royal headpiece. Preserve the stated count without converting to a modern currency.
A heap of dung or refuse supporting the animals in Orlando’s comparison; no inherited Biblical scene or animal species is imported.
Outer plant coverings eaten with the hogs in Orlando’s prodigal-son allusion. No particular species is asserted.
Youngest in age within the stated family; a relative age, not a fixed Unta number or small bodily size.
Older by relative age in the brother comparison; not a council officer or an assertion of moral superiority.
The trained handling and movements taught to horses, source manage; distinct from management of a household or holding political office.
A household or estate worker with whom Orlando is made to feed, source hind; never the female deer.
The insult in the brothers’ quarrel retains both base social birth and moral baseness. Orlando denies low birth and turns the charge against the shared father’s defamer.
Nominal growth, excessive growth metaphorically applied to Orlando’s rebellion by Oliver; a growth he proposes to dose with medicine, not an offensive smell or official rank.
Dose or treat with medicine, Oliver’s threatening metaphor for suppressing his brother. It is his intention, not a narrator’s diagnosis or an actual prescription.
The contemptuous be-naught dismissal in Oliver’s make/mar exchange. Nothingness as insult, not numerical zero in a reckoning.

Force a person out of a ruler’s domain. This ordinary political sense is independent of earlier plague imagery.

senses.definition: An infant’s bed, the cradle from which the cousins were raised together. Native infant + bed replaces the unjustified inherited cradil imitation for this new work; earlier sealed editions are unchanged.
England in the Robin Hood comparison. Reviewed promotion of the existing permitted place-name stem, with a clean printed label instead of its internal historical lookup key.
A bodily feature or contour in Rosalind’s distinction between innate Nature and worldly Fortune; not a political boundary.

The dialogue’s teasing designation of a fool by nature, contrasted with cultivated wit and the professional entertainer. Native nature + fool retains the recurrent Nature family; no narrator diagnosis of Touchstone is asserted.
A stone for sharpening an edge, extended to sharpening wit through the fool’s apparent dullness. Native sharpen + stone; the same sharpening image is repeated deliberately.

Critical personal reproach, source taxation in Celia’s warning to the fool. It is not levying money or an Unta quantity.

senses.definition: A masonry spreading blade, invoked by Celia for language applied clumsily or thickly. Native wall + spread + blade; no actual masonry work is performed onstage.
The whole pair, keeping the existing Unta two + all formation. Human-reviewed quantitative both, without replacing it by an Arabic digit or losing its inclusive force.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: le_beau_courtier

senses.definition: The courtier who describes the wrestling. The supplied compound personal name is retained phonetically; Monsieur remains a native courtesy title.
A gathered mound, extended by Celia to the fool’s supposed store of knowledge. No exact amount or textile nap is implied.
Nominal conversion of dull: slowness of wit, contrasted with the sharpening whetstone. Retains the repeated native dull root without importing the Lethe stupor context.
The bird whose feeding of its young supplies Celia’s news simile. Reviewed promotion of the native bird-kind stem; distinct from a turtle dove.
Cut off a train of speech or reasoning. Native off + cut forms an inflecting interruption verb, retaining the cutting image without an ambiguous particle stranded outside an agent noun.
A human rib injured in wrestling. Reviewed anatomical side-bone sense, without importing the earlier Biblical removal or creation event.
Nominal growth of a young man’s body in Le Beau’s description; physical development, not rank vegetation or social promotion.

A written public notice, the written sense of bills invoked by Rosalind’s formal announcement. The English weapon/notice homonym is recorded as a wordplay loss, not silently assigned to the native notice root.
Receive a person into the family as an heir by choice rather than birth. Native choose + heir made verbal; Orlando rejects this hypothetical relation to Frederick.
Envious in Celia’s reproach means spiteful or malicious in disposition. Contextual extension of envy, distinct from merely wanting another person’s possessions.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: rowland_short

senses.definition: The shortened Sir Rowland address to the same Rowland de Boys; no new person or unprinted family-name expansion.
A practice target for mock mounted combat, invoked as a lifeless stand-in for the speechless Orlando. Native exercise + target; not a living opponent or an actual object brought onstage.
Humorous in Le Beau’s warning means governed by changing moods, not funny. Native change + will describes this unstable inclination.
A clinging prickly seed head in the women’s garment and heart metaphor. Native thorn + seed replaces unjustified source-sounding buril in this new work; no exact plant species asserted.
An ordinary day of labour contrasted with holiday pleasure; native work + day. No assigned weekday or Unta calendar interval.
A festive day free from ordinary labour in Celia’s flirtation joke; native rest + day, not a specific religious feast or fixed weekly date.
The brown earth pigment used to darken Celia’s face for disguise. Native brown + earth; not a change of ancestry or an assertion of modern pigment chemistry.
The source curtal-ax is a short broad sword or cutlass carried at the thigh, not a woodcutting axe. Native short + sword; no invented blade dimensions.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: ganymede_alias

senses.definition: The name of Jove’s page chosen by Rosalind for her disguise. The allusion and assumed name are explicit; she is not asserted to be the mythic figure.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: aliena_alias

senses.definition: Celia’s chosen alias, a personal name with an exile/estrangement implication stated in the dialogue. Keep the phonetic name; do not introduce an ordinary foreign adjective into native vocabulary.
Gentle or polished outward manner, which Frederick suspiciously attributes to Rosalind. Nominal smooth; does not itself assert deceit or a physically smooth surface.
The Duke’s territorial dominion taken by Frederick, source dukedom. Native duke + land keeps the rank explicit instead of replacing it with a generic principality.

The primordial Adam named in the Duke’s allusion to Adam’s penalty, not the old servant Adam present elsewhere in this play. Reviewed personal-name identity; the disputed interpretation of the penalty is recorded separately.
Adverse circumstances in the Duke’s claimed sweet uses of adversity; native adverse-time, without importing the former Psalm speaker or a new calendar period.
Hunted game meat, here associated with the deer the Duke considers hunting. Retains the meat-for-animal metonymy without naming a modern deer species.
An instructive moral or religious address, figuratively found in stones by the Duke; native teach + speech, with no literal new preacher in the forest.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: branch + arrow + head

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: branch + arrow + head
lexicon.label: forked_arrowhead

senses.definition: The forked heads of hunting arrows, not the deer’s antlers. Native branch + arrow + head retains the weapon shape without supplying an unprinted dimension.
The fleshy upper hindquarter of the deer, a contextual extension of hip; not merely an isolated pelvic bone or a human thigh.
The male deer wounded in the hunter’s aim and watched by Jaques. Native male + deer, without adding species, age or antler count.
An explicit instructive comparison in Jaques’s interpretation of the weeping deer. The native comparison noun is specialized to rhetorical likeness, not a numerical equation.
Substantial thought or subject matter in conversation, the content the Duke expects from Jaques’s melancholy. Extends content beyond a written document; not physical material.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: amiens_lord

senses.definition: The lord accompanying Duke Senior and singing in the forest, named Amiens or Lord of Amiens. A character’s title-name, not a newly visited city.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: jaques_courtier

senses.definition: The melancholy courtier with Duke Senior, distinct from Orlando’s school-going brother Jaques and the pilgrimage Saint Jaques. No identity qualifier prints in the name.
Payment earned through work or service, Adam’s savings from serving Orlando’s father. Distinct from hiring a worker as a verb or a gift; no additional monetary amount is implied.
Cut back cultivated growth to encourage it, applied by Orlando to himself as a rotten tree. Keeps the native branch-cut verb without importing the earlier vineyard or calendar law.
Cultivating and caring for plant growth, Orlando’s image for Adam’s support. The native field-work compound does not imply marriage or a new plot of land.
A place where a person sleeps or stays, the lodging Oliver plans to burn. No extra room count or building plan.

The small seed-eating bird category called sparrow in Adam’s providence allusion. Native seed + bird is a lexicalized category, not a claim that every seed-eating bird is a sparrow; replaces unjustified sparil in this new work only.

An attractive or admirable personal quality, the graces that expose Orlando to envy. Nominal attractive grace, distinct from a title of address and from divine favour; the following holy-traitor metaphor remains explicit.
Advancement in social standing or office sought by self-interested servants. Native rank + rise; does not insert a particular rank or employment contract.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: hisperia_attendant

senses.definition: The Princess’s gentlewoman who reports overhearing the cousins. Her belief that Orlando travelled with them is a reported inference, not a true stage direction or a new identity for another attendant.

lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_bh_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 17; Unta 15.

lexicon.etymology: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked
lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_ia_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 80; Unta 68.

citations.locator: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked

lexicon.etymology: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked
lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_h_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 7; Unta 7.
The fitted torso garment in Rosalind’s masculine disguise. Native body + garment identifies this source clothing category without making its name a numerical assertion of two layers.
Leg clothing worn with the doublet, contrasted with the petticoat. Not a liquid-carrying pipe, and no modern cut or fabric is specified.

An intersecting cross-shaped mark or object, invoked through the stamp on source-culture coins in Touchstone’s joke. Native cross + mark retains the shape; its monetary implication follows the purse clause. Not a new native religious doctrine.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: wash + wood + beat

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: wash + wood + beat
lexicon.label: laundry_batler

senses.definition: The washing implement used to beat clothes, not a butter churn or an insect. Native wash + wood + beat names its function; no invented dimensions or particular wood.
A milk-giving teat of the cow, source dugs, kissed in Touchstone’s extravagant memory. Native milk + breast; not a generic wound or an act of digging.
Draw milk from an animal. Reviewed verbal conversion of the native milk noun; no processing method or measure is added.
Skin cracked or roughened, source chopped hands. Contextual cracked-skin modifier; the hands have not been cut off.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: round + seed + cover

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: round + seed + cover
lexicon.label: pea_pod_native

senses.definition: The pea-pod used as a surrogate beloved in Touchstone’s story. Native round + seed + cover is a lexicalized plant category, not all round-seed coverings. The odd taking of two pods from this personification is retained rather than silently corrected into peas or an added plant.
A seed-bearing plant pod or its enclosing shell, source cods. Native seed + cover; the source count is two pods, not two individual peas.

Context-bound death-root intensification in Touchstone’s mortal in folly: excessive rather than a claim that every lover dies. Retains the death-family echo of ordinary mortal in the preceding clause; an authored literary extension, not a universal rule changing the ordinary mortality adjective.
The front bony part of the lower leg struck in Touchstone’s wit metaphor. Native leg + bone lexicalization names this region without asserting that every leg bone is a shin.
The small rural dwelling offered with pasture and flock. Native small + house; no implied new room count, freehold law or modern building plan.
Shelter or enclosure associated with the sheep flock. Native sheep + house, distinct from the shepherd’s personal dwelling and from a coat of clothing.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: sheep + hair + cut

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: sheep + hair + cut
lexicon.label: shear_fleece

senses.definition: Remove wool from the sheep by cutting. Native wool + cut avoids the old unsupported source-like shirël; the source contrasts tending the flock with taking its yield, without specifying a tool design.
One who tends and feeds the flock, the source feeder in Corin’s promise. Native feed + person; do not silently adopt another edition’s factor or assert that Corin has already purchased the property.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: corin_shepherd

senses.definition: The older shepherd who advises Silvius and helps the disguised cousins. Distinct semantic identity from the Corin name invoked in another play’s pastoral allusion.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: silvius_shepherd

senses.definition: The young shepherd devoted to Phoebe in As You Like It; not an ancient Roman namesake.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: phoebe_shepherdess

senses.definition: The shepherdess loved by Silvius. Distinct from the moon deity Phoebe, despite the same permitted phonetic personal-name form.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: jane_smile

senses.definition: The woman named in Touchstone’s recollection. The complete personal name is adapted phonetically; Smile is not falsely translated as an ordinary action in the name.
The bodily and mental animation exhausted by travel in Rosalind and Touchstone’s exchange. Contextual vitality, conventionally plural in this contrast; not multiple ghosts or a count of souls.
A grouped section of a song or poem; native song + group. Distinct from an individual line. The ordinary term against Jaques’s deliberately distorted term in Act 2 Scene 5.

citations.locator: Authored local distortion of native lilgur; source naming joke.

lexicon.etymology: Authored local distortion of native lilgur; source naming joke.
lexicon.label: stanza_misnamed

senses.definition: Jaques’s uncertain naming of a song stanza: lilgrur, a local distortion of native lilgur, song-group. Authored comic sound substitution for stanzo/stanzos, not a productive plural rule or an ordinary foreign loan. The English ending joke is adapted, not reproduced exactly.

The dog-faced ape/baboon category of Jaques’s comparison of ceremonial courtesies. Native dog + monkey is lexicalized here; no claim of a dog-primate hybrid or precise modern species. Avoids unsupported ape/apen sound copying.
Ceremonial expressions of politeness or thanks in Jaques’s contemptuous comparison. Contextual courtesy, not necessarily a factual praise of merit.
A table prepared for eating or drinking. Contextual extension of the native table/surface noun; cover means lay the table in this scene, not conceal the Duke or tree.
Inclined to disputation, source disputable describing the Duke. Native argument in a characteristic modifier use; not a claim that his existence is disputed.
The faculty or exercise of devising verse, Jaques’s invention. In despite of it preserves his self-disparaging paradox; does not assert an independently known motive for writing the parody.

citations.locator: Authored nonce blend: come + clipped/reordered fool and circle; not claimed Greek or a historical form.

lexicon.etymology: Authored nonce blend: come + clipped/reordered fool and circle; not claimed Greek or a historical form.
lexicon.label: mock_invocation

senses.definition: An opaque comic call replacing source Ducdame: authored native root-play from come, fool and circle, with clipping and rearrangement. These are construction rationale, not an etymology asserted by the characters. Jaques claims it is Greek; the translation does not certify that claim or settle the disputed source word.
A summoning call or formula, including Jaques’s claimed Greek call to gather fools. No divine recipient is added; distinct from the god-call term for religious invocation.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: mixed + colour + cloth

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: mixed + colour + cloth
lexicon.label: motley_cloth

senses.definition: The mixed-colour fabric or costume associated with the licensed fool. Native mixed + colour + cloth, lexicalized as the costume category. Not a new character name or a specified count of colours; the narrative’s irony does not become a narrator claim that all wearers are unintelligent.
The breathing organ, Jaques’s lungs in his crowing-laughter image. Native breath + chamber. A lexicalized anatomical term, not every chamber containing air; no new physiological theory is asserted.
Draw or speak an exemplary lesson, here about time and human life. Reviewed verbal conversion of the native moral/lesson noun; not condemn someone as immoral.

citations.locator: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked

lexicon.etymology: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked
lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_bb_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 11; Unta B.
Cut open for examination; figuratively expose the wise man’s folly in Jaques’s speech. Native cut + look. No actual surgery or corpse is introduced.
A token used for reckoning, offered as a trivial wager by Jaques. Native reckon + token; not a serving surface or an assigned cash amount.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: lust + liberty + person

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: lust + liberty + person
lexicon.label: libertine_person

senses.definition: A person given to unrestrained sensual living in the Duke’s accusation. Native lust + liberty + person, not the historical named synagogue group or a modern political affiliation.
Showy clothing or personal display, source bravery; native adorn + garment. Distinct from courage, and no unstated specific item or price.

The source community’s Christian worship building. Native faith + house replaces unsupported chiren in this new translation. The context specifies the institution; this does not merge every native faith-house into that historical religion.
Socially cultivated courtesy and good manners, contrasted with Orlando’s desperate threats. No requirement of aristocratic birth or modern citizenship is asserted.
Cultivated upbringing and good breeding, source nurture in Orlando’s defence. Not merely feeding, and not a claim that he was raised at a particular modern school.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: neck + water + bird

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: neck + water + bird
lexicon.label: wild_goose_native

senses.definition: The wild goose in Jaques’s unclaimed-criticism comparison. Native neck + water + bird is a lexicalized category, not a diagnosis of a modern species or every waterbird; avoids unsupported source-like gansil.
Female deer in Orlando’s comparison of himself seeking food for Adam. Native female + deer; not a claim that Orlando or Adam is literally an animal.
A place of dramatic performance, native play + house; the universal theater is a metaphor for the world, not an asserted building surrounding it.
A role performed by an actor, a contextual part of a dramatic performance; neither a numerical fraction nor a body part.
A weak plaintive infant cry. Native weak + call, lexicalized for this vocal action; no imitation of the English sound is claimed.
Complain in a plaintive tone, the reluctant schoolboy’s action. Contextual extension of native voiced complaint.
Carrying bag associated here with schooling, native school + bag. Does not add a book inventory or a particular strap construction.
Hair of the brow above the eye, the object of the lover’s extravagant ballad; distinct from the whole forehead.
The large spotted wild-cat category called pard in the source. Native spot + cat, lexicalized rather than denoting any marked domestic cat; no new species or invented beard anatomy asserted.
A castrated domestic male fowl raised for eating, native cut + cock as a lexicalized food category. Not any injured cock and not a new productive castration morpheme.
Regularly arranged according to convention, here the magistrate’s beard cut. Does not denote a formal proof or official legal enactment.

The conventional old-man stage figure represented by the source pantaloon. Native old + mask names the theatrical role without borrowing its Italian name. Its thinness, slippers and spectacles are separately stated in the passage.
Soft easily worn footwear, native soft + shoe, worn by the stage old man. No material or indoor location is added.
Eyeglasses aiding sight, native sight + glass as a lexicalized implement. One noun denotes the apparatus; no unsupported extra numerical count of lenses is inserted.
A high vocal register, native high + voice. Source childish treble is not three, threefold, a musical interval, or a specified frequency.
The evergreen prickly-leaved holly of the song, native thorn + leaf as a lexicalized plant category. Does not assert that all thorny plants are holly or add unmentioned fruit to the song.
Failure of gratitude, native not + gratitude as a lexicalized disposition. Distinct from the mere absence of a spoken thank-you in a particular moment.

Water freezing or forming a distorted icy surface, the source waters warp. A contextual frozen-water image, not an assertion of a particular crystal structure; the English weave/distort resonance is not fully reproduced.

citations.locator: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked

lexicon.etymology: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked
lexicon.label: unta_ordinal_g_over_b

senses.definition: Exact ordinal quantity 6; Unta 6.
The action of entering, especially a performer’s arrival onstage. Nominal use of native enter, distinct from a physical door or a fee for admission.
Pretence as an activity or condition, nominal use of native feign. In the song, friendship is said to be pretence, not an agent that pretends on somebody’s behalf.
Official valuation of property for seizure, source make an extent upon house and lands. Native value + seize names this legal act, not spatial extent or a new modern statute.
Inquiry or wisdom concerning causes and life, native cause + know. Touchstone’s broad question admits Corin’s practical maxims; no modern academic department is imposed.
Lean or scant in provision, the spare pastoral life that suits Touchstone’s disposition but not his appetite. Native little + means, not spare as forgive or rescue.
Condemnation to divine punishment, nominal use of native damn in Touchstone’s deliberately specious syllogism. A character’s assertion, not the translator’s verdict.
Adult female sheep, native female + sheep, distinct from the male ram and young lamb.
Adult uncastrated male sheep, native male + sheep. Animal category, not a siege weapon or a newly invented proper name.

Castrated male sheep, native cut + sheep as a lexicalized livestock category. Bell-wether here has a bell and leads sheep; retain Touchstone’s deliberately incongruous bawdy personification, not a biologically corrected ram.

Dark sticky tar used in the source sheep-care practice. Native pitch-family material noun extended to this named substance; no claim that every pitch or resin has identical composition, and no treatment recipe supplied.

The animal-derived aromatic secretion used to scent courtiers’ hands. Native cat + odour as a lexicalized substance name reflecting the source category. Not ordinary house-cat scent, and Touchstone’s uncleanly flux characterization stays his judgment.
A cutting into flesh in Touchstone’s mock healing wish, nominal cut. No actual operation takes place and no anatomical procedure is specified.

Unpractised or unformed in wit, with tender/sore flesh available in the adjacent incision joke. Contextual extension of native raw; the source English overlap with uncooked food is not claimed exact native homophony.
Sexual joining of animals for breeding, native body + join. Does not turn the shepherd’s animal husbandry into a literal human sexual act.
Herded domestic animals, native herd + beast. Source cattle here includes the sheep just named, not exclusively cows.
A pairing of animals for breeding, contextual nominal match in Touchstone’s parody of unsuitable marriage. Not a numerical equality or a lighted match.
Evening meal, native evening + food. Replaces the unsupported ordinary sound-copy supen in this new work only; no earlier edition is rewritten.

An ordered row or procession, the supplied butter-women’s rank going to market. Retains rank rather than adopting an editor’s rack or rate emendation; its comparison to monotonous verse is contextual, not a social rank.
Put an inner layer in a garment, native inside + cloth. Touchstone applies the same term to slender Rosalind in an innuendo; not the pictorial lined of the earlier poem.
A wheeled carrier of loads, the harvest-cart image in Touchstone’s bawdy verse. Contextual native wagon; no exact wheel count or public punishment is silently added.
A horse’s rapid running gait, native horse + run, figuratively applied to verse rhythm. False gallop preserves the rough or affected progression; no fixed native metrical pattern is claimed.

The medlar fruit of Rosalind’s graft/rot/ripe jest, native fruit + soft as a lexicalized fruit-category name. Not a generic word for every soft fruit; its sexual insinuation and paradoxical earliest wording are source-specific.
A hand-span, the source bodily length image enclosing an entire lifetime. Same native hand + measure as the historical witness, reviewed for later use without importing a fixed metric length.

The finest concentrated essence, distilled from every spirit in the poem. Native essence in an explicit extraction sense. The word’s fifth-element background is not an assertion of five spirits or one fifth of each spirit in this passage.
A deliberative assembly, here the imagined heavenly council devising Rosalind. Native council, not a specifically Christian ecclesiastical organization.
A member of the local worshipping congregation in Rosalind’s mock-sermon address. Native faith + person as a contextual congregation role, not a new denominational identity.
Carried possessions accompanying departure, native carry-goods promoted from the historical witness. In the stock military leave-taking phrase, not a wheeled carriage or the insult for a person.
A pouch carrying small provisions, native carry-bag promoted from the historical witness. Not script, written language or a form of money.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: carry + bag + thing

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: carry + bag + thing
lexicon.label: scrippage_play

senses.definition: Touchstone’s coined echo of scrip in bag-and-baggage/scrip-and-scrippage: native carry-bag-thing. An authored local comic derivative, not a productive grammatical rule or an ordinary English loan.

A rhythmic unit of verse, extended from the same native foot noun as the body part. This shared form carries the feet-bearing/limping joke; it does not certify that the native translation has the source’s exact scansion.
A palm tree, source place where Rosalind found the poem. The native historical tree term is promoted with its tree meaning; no specific species or forest relocation is invented.
Rat, the gnawing rodent in Rosalind’s Irish-rat reincarnation joke. Native grain + tooth as a lexicalized animal category, not any grain-eater or a claim that a rat is a tooth.
Colour or visible appearance of the face, native face + colour. Good my complexion retains the source apostrophe and its interpretive uncertainty; do not emend it to Hudson’s complicator.
A portable container for liquid, promoted with the same native liquid-bag form. Source bottle is not assigned a material or volume absent from the passage.

A cork closure for a bottle, native wood + close as a lexicalized stopper name. Its bark-derived material is part of the category; the compound does not assert it is cut solid timber or provide manufacturing instructions.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: rosalinda_poem

senses.definition: The poem’s expanded name for Rosalind, the same woman. Preserve the supplied final vowel as a poetic name variant, not a new person.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: atalanta_heroine

senses.definition: The mythic heroine named among the qualities distilled for Rosalind. Her better part remains unspecified; no disputed interpretation is substituted for the phrase.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: pythagoras_philosopher

senses.definition: The philosopher in Rosalind’s playful reference to transmigration. The joke does not establish that he knew an Irish rat or that Rosalind literally remembers a prior life.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: ireland_place

senses.definition: Ireland as the rat’s source affiliation in Rosalind’s allusion. Permitted place-name adaptation, not an ordinary borrowed adjective.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: western_ind_place

senses.definition: Western Ind in the poem’s east-to-west sweep, commonly understood as the West Indies. Native west plus the permitted India/Ind name; no modern border or journey is asserted.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: south_sea_place

senses.definition: The South Sea in Rosalind’s oceanic discovery metaphor, commonly the Pacific. Native historical south plus sea forms the geographical name; not a travel instruction or a newly invented sea.
Hold in high value or esteem, verbal conversion of native value. Distinct from the prize as a reward won or sought.
Significance or consequence in that is no matter. Figurative native weight, distinct from material substance or a specific measurable mass.

Falter or repeat in speaking, the narrow-mouthed-bottle image of Rosalind’s impatient request. Reviewed promotion of the native speech-stumble formation. Not a medical diagnosis, an insult added by the translator, or permission to delete source repetition.

A repeated sung response or refrain, the song’s borne burden. A later literary extension of native burden that preserves Celia’s song/load image. Distinct from the unsupported ordinary loan koren; it does not imply an actual heavy object or a fixed count of repetitions.

Religious instruction in questions and answers, native faith + teach as a lexicalized instructional genre. Celia compares Rosalind’s many questions to this format; not a named doctrinal text or merely any lesson.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: gargantua_giant

senses.definition: The giant Gargantua named in Celia’s exaggerated request for a mouth large enough for all her answers. Permitted personal-name adaptation; no additional episode from Rabelais is inserted.

The source Christian baptism/naming occasion in Orlando’s answer about Rosalind’s name. Reviewed native ritual-washing term; do not assign an unprinted age or mode of baptism, or reduce the occasion to merely painting or washing an object.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: gold + work + person

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: gold + work + person
lexicon.label: goldsmith_craft

senses.definition: A worker in gold, especially jewellery in Jaques’s ring-motto joke. Native gold + work + person; the wives remain distinct participants, not substituted for the craftsmen.
An attending foot-servant, the impudent role Rosalind says she will play. Native foot + servant, not a character called Lackey or a borrowed class label.
Move at an easy smooth gait, native smooth + step. In Rosalind’s personified time passage it contrasts with a jarring trot and rapid gallop; no count of strides is inserted or speed order inverted.
Move at the horse’s rapid running gait; verbal use of the existing horse-run gait noun. Time gallops for the condemned thief in the source comparison, even if he walks softly.

Latin, the named language lacking in the priest’s learning. Reviewed promotion of the geographic Rome + native language label; no assertion about the native Vayrshemon script, church liturgy reform, or precise historical dialect.
The hanging execution structure approached by the thief. Reviewed native hang-wood category; no new dimensions or claim about the stranger’s guilt is added.
A period when courts conduct their business, native law + time. The periods in the lawyers’ joke, not an arbitrary school term or a specified statutory calendar.
The interval when courts are not sitting, native law + rest. Source lawyers sleep between legal terms; not a modern holiday package or the assertion that legal work always ceases.
Threads or trimming at a garment edge. Promoted native garment-fringe form for the forest-edge/petticoat simile, without importing the earlier historical verse’s ritual instruction.
The personified mock address Signior Love, directed to Orlando. Native love receives proper-name Maxima in this epithet; no new person or foreign ordinary word is introduced.
The answering mock address Monsieur Melancholy, directed to Jaques. Native melancholy receives proper-name Maxima in the epithet; not a diagnosis or a new onstage character.
A lyric poem of praise, native praise + song. The tree-hung odes exalt Rosalind; no unstated ancient metrical pattern is claimed.
A plaintive lyric or lament, native sorrow + song. Orlando’s love elegies need not announce a death; no funeral event is invented.
A recurrent daily fever, native day + fever, used for love’s recurring fits. Keeps the daily interval without assigning a new number of fits per day or making a real clinical diagnosis.
A head covering or cap in the lover’s disordered attire. Promoted native head-cloth without the historical priestly context or a modern gendered bonnet shape.
A strip or binding band on clothing, here around a bonnet. Same native cloth-bind formation, without the injury/wound meaning of bandage or the unsupported group word banel.
A button fastening a garment, native round + bind as a lexicalized clothing fastener. Does not require a round geometric shape for every token or import a digital UI button.
Expel saliva from the mouth, the scornful gesture in Rosalind’s claimed treatment. Reviewed native mouth-expel form; no speech or vomiting substituted.

The secluded religious way of life in Rosalind’s story, native faith + alone. Keeps the religious withdrawal as well as solitude, without naming an order or asserting the alleged patient actually existed.

Knowledge and practice of courtly society and manners, source courtship in the supposed uncle’s biography. Distinct from courting a beloved, though the following falling-in-love statement keeps the source association.
An individual metal monetary token, native metal + money. Distinguishes a coin from an unbounded sum; its denomination is specified separately, including the source half-penny coins.

Cultivated in manners through life among settled society, source inland man. Contextual modifier from the native upbringing term, contrasted with remote forest life; no exact geographical interior, court rank or modern city is assigned.

The feminine or soft behaviour in Ganymede’s caricature of an inconstant youth, using native woman-soft. A reviewed dramatic manner-description rather than the earlier historical hostile-list category; no modern identity or specific sexual act is asserted.
The goat herded by Audrey, reviewed native animal-category form. No ritual scapegoat role or unprinted sex is added.

Form or fashioned appearance in Touchstone’s feature/features exchange. The native form noun leaves bodily appearance and a fashioned literary piece available; the disputed poem reading is not silently imposed as certain.
Poetry as an art or generic composition, a collective non-count sense of native verse. No exact count of lines or specific classical metre is asserted.
Roofing of dry stalks, native straw + roof. The poor house in the Jove allusion; no additional host names or construction method is inserted.
Sugar, native reed + sweet as a lexicalized sweetener category, contrasted with honey. Not a loan and not a claim that every sweet reed produces the same commodity.

The local parish cleric, Sir Oliver Martext’s office. Native community + priest distinguishes the source local church role without inventing a modern denomination or turning the clerical Sir into knighthood.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: small + faith + house

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: small + faith + house
lexicon.label: chapel_worship

senses.definition: A local or smaller place of worship, native small + faith-house. Kept distinct from the forest and from the church to which Jaques directs the couple; no new physical building is added onstage.
The controlling part of a horse’s bridle, a specified native bridle sense in the restraints/desires comparison. No modern tack specification or kerbstone meaning.
Birds touching or rubbing their bills in paired caress, native kiss as an explicit animal-action extension. Not a financial bill, a weapon or a new courtship claim about all birds.
Joined wooden wall lining, native wood + wall. The carpentry comparison for a badly made marriage; not a specific wood species or an invented modern joinery method.
A board or panel used in that lining, native wood + piece. A member that may shrink/warp in the marriage simile, not a software control.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: audrey_goatherd

senses.definition: Audrey, the goatherd courted by Touchstone; no unprinted full saint-name expansion.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: ovid_poet

senses.definition: The Roman poet named in Touchstone’s exile comparison. Keep the supplied name and the character’s claim about Goths rather than silently repairing it to Getae.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: goth_people

senses.definition: Short address to the same Oliver Martext, including the song joke. No namesake qualifier appears in the reading text.
Earlier-developed understanding, source forward child; native early + know. Not physical forward motion or an added age.
A dirty or careless woman in the foul/slut distinction. Native dirty + woman; no prostitution or specific sexual act is asserted.
Dirty or careless habits, native dirty + manner. Retains Touchstone’s distinction from plain looks rather than automatically translating the insult as sexual misconduct.
The assembled company at a wedding, contrasted with horned beasts; no formal council or parliament is added.
Green wood as still fresh and undried, the carpentry sense of native green. Not painted wood or the human inexperience sense of unseasoned.
Judas the betrayer in Celia’s hair and kiss joke, with the source short name only. Distinct from other Judas/Judah identities; no reference label or Iscariot is added to the printed name.
The chestnut colour in Celia’s teasing reply, native chestnut + colour. A conventional colour comparison, not an asserted tree species or a replacement of the source brown/red contrast.
Fine, splendid or showy, with ironic force in Celia’s repeated brave/bravely. Distinct from the narrower courageous sense; the same native stem is repeated throughout the boast parody.

lexicon.label: diana_goddess_full

senses.definition: Full Diana form for the classical goddess in Celia’s chastity joke, corresponding to existing Dian. Not the human Diana in All’s Well; no Bible reference suffix prints.
Urge a horse with the rider’s spur. Reviewed noun-to-action conversion, preserving the source one-sided riding error without an unstated race or military charge.
Visible radiance or luminous flush, here the red glow of proud scorn. Native light sense, avoiding a source-sounding ordinary glow loan; no actual fire is added.
Observe with attention, source mark the enacted pageant. Visual-attention use of native look, not stamping a physical mark.
A small pointed fastening pin, native needle + bind, able to leave a scratch in Phoebe’s comparison. Not an added weapon or a modern safety pin mechanism.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: glass + small + round

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: glass + small + round
lexicon.label: bugle_bead

senses.definition: The dark glass bead used as the comparison for Phoebe’s eyes; native glass + small + round. Not a brass instrument, bison or an asserted jewellery design.
The rich upper part of milk, native milk + top, in the pale-cheek image. No cosmetic preparation or modern manufacturing process.
Gather crop remnants after the main harvest, reused in Silvius’s small-share love metaphor. No Biblical ritual or specific legal entitlement is transferred.
A cereal seed-head, native grain-head, here broken remnants after harvesting; not an anatomical ear or specifically maize.
Favour shown to a lover, the grace Silvius lacks. Ordinary relational extension without making Phoebe a deity or asserting a doctrine of salvation.
Omission or failure to answer immediately, the source omittance. Nominal use of native leave-out; distinguished from acquittal or repayment.
Release from an obligation or claim, contrasted proverbially with omitting an immediate response. Nominal sense, not a completed criminal trial.
The axe used by the executioner in Silvius’s comparison. Reviewed extension of native wood-cut tool to the same weapon/tool category, without adding a type of blade.
The cardinal south, including the misty south wind in Rosalind’s simile. Not a particular modern country or the named South Sea.
Ease from sorrow or distress, the relief Silvius asks should follow pity; not food or a relief sculpture.
Greedy desire or wanting more, nominal use of native covet in Phoebe’s response. The accusation is her rhetoric, not the narrator’s judgement.
The red coloration of a lip, nominal colour use of native red; no added blood or injury.
Season or accompany with sauce, used figuratively for answering with bitter words. Explicit action use of native taste-liquid; no actual food preparation is added to the scene.
An upright wooden post in Rosalind’s joke about silent sadness, native wood + stand. Not the existing post verb meaning relay-horse travel.
A habitually drunken person in the comparison with excessive melancholy or laughter. Reviewed native drunk-person, without importing the historical accusation context.
A person practising music, native music + person, in Jaques’s list of kinds of melancholy.
Governed by fancy or imagination, the musician’s melancholy. Contextual modifier of native fancy, not excellent or a claim of supernatural events.
Draw a constituent out of a source, the medicinal-mixture metaphor for Jaques’s experience. Not copying written excerpts or introducing an actual pharmaceutical procedure.
Marked by a prevailing mood or temperament, Jaques’s humorous sadness. Native mood modifier; not comical or amusing. The possible bodily-humour background remains a metaphor, not a diagnosis.
Knowledge or impressions gained by lived encounters and travel. Nominal use of native experience; Jaques claims it as the profit of his journey.
Place or country of birth, the origin a fashionable traveller disowns in Rosalind’s caricature. Reviewed native birth-place, not the Christian festival.
Lisp or affect altered articulation in the traveller caricature, native tongue + soft. A lexical speech action; not the existing plant-shoot slip, and not a diagnosis or an invented specific accent.

The Venetian gondola category, native city + boat. Its source-cultural referent is retained without borrowing the ordinary foreign word or adding Venice to the spoken line. No modern motor or specific dimensions are asserted.

A wife’s settled provision to support her if widowed, native widow + right. The snail’s house is jokingly called a better jointure; not the bride’s dowry, social rank or a promise of a particular modern legal arrangement.
Strike or pat with the hand, native hand + beat, here Cupid’s touch upon the shoulder. Not applause or the arrow striking the heart.
A look or cast of countenance, source better leer. Nominal native look; not necessarily a lascivious expression or a taunt about poor eyesight.

Overgrown or excessive, with an unfavourable implication in honesty ranker than wit. Native growth modifier preserves the exaggerated comparison without substituting social rank or committing solely to rotten smell.

lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_gaaa_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 6000; Unta 3580.
The ape in Rosalind’s novelty-loving comparison. Reviewed native animal-category stem, distinct from the next monkey term; no modern species claim and no ordinary ape/apen borrowing.
The parrot whose noisy cries are compared with a wife’s clamour before rain; native speech + bird as a lexicalized animal category, not every calling bird.

The hyena invoked for its laugh-like cry, native bone + tooth as a lexicalized animal category. The comparison stays a character’s image; no particular modern species or hybrid with a dog is asserted.
Fond of new things and changing fashions, source newfangled; native new + desire. Not newly manufactured or merely young.
The opening for a key, native key + hole, in the escaping-wit image. No modern lock mechanism is specified.
An opening window, native turn + window, in the escaping-wit sequence. Keeps the hinged-window category without an unsupported source-sounding kasel form.
The smoke passage from a house, native smoke-way, reused for wit escaping with smoke. Not a window or a newly added fire onstage.
Feed and nurture a child, with the mother’s milk-feeding sense available. Reviewed native milk-feed; not hospital care or the noun caregiver.
Bring up or form a child through care and training, source breed it like a fool. Explicit verbal extension of native upbringing; not beget a new child.
A very small mark or part, here any smallest part of a promise. Native small-sign, without asserting that the source sign is a Thimfora letter or adding a script-specific character.

Emotionally emphatic or impassioned, used mockingly in Rosalind’s pathetical break-promise. Native passion modifier follows the impassioned reading; other editors suggest miserable/pitiful, so this is a recorded interpretive choice, not a claim of unanimity.
Melancholy thought in Cupid begot of thought, native thought + sorrow. Retains thinking as well as sorrow, distinct from purely rational calculation.
Capricious or impulsive temper in Cupid’s mock conception, nominal native change-will. The bodily-humour image is recorded; it does not assert a surgical organ or prescribe a theory of medicine.
Measure depth, especially of water, in Rosalind’s fathom/bay image. Native water-measure; not audible sound or reporting a known numerical depth.
