senses.definition: The historical North African regional name qualifying the source pigeon. Permitted geographical name; no claim about a modern border or a type of human character.

citations.locator: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.

lexicon.etymology: Author-permitted phonetic adaptation of a personal name.
lexicon.label: portugal_place

senses.definition: Portugal in the Bay of Portugal comparison. Preserve the geographical label without replacing it with a guessed modern bay or a measured depth.
The stringed weapon used with arrows in Celia’s remark about Orlando. Reviewed native curved-string bow; not the bodily action of bowing or the rainbow extension.
A task on which someone is sent, here Silvius carrying Phoebe’s letter. Native send-work; not the contents of the message or an assertion that he knows them.
Openly challenge in hostility. Native challenge-against, promoted for Rosalind’s rhetorical description of Phoebe’s letter; distinct from its actually affectionate wording.
Divine nature or condition in Phoebe’s god-disguised-as-shepherd conceit. Native god-state; no biblical person, Trinity doctrine or exact divine number imported.
A person’s handwriting, the written hand in Rosalind’s physical-hand/authorship joke. Shares the native hand form deliberately; does not assert that Phoebe’s handwriting was independently identified.
A building stone that can be cut or dressed freely, used for the colour of Phoebe’s hand. Native cut-stone category; no exact mineral, hue or liberated-stone reading imposed.
The prevailing tone or drift of a written message, here Silvius’s guess at anger from Phoebe’s behaviour. Contextual native manner; not a musical vocal range.

Rosalind’s local coined verb for being treated in Phoebe’s supposedly cruel manner. The personal name plus native act preserves the name-to-verb joke. A source-bound theatrical coinage, not ordinary imported vocabulary or a productive insult for unrelated women.

Land at the outskirts or cleared margin of the forest, where Oliver seeks the sheepcote. Native forest-edge; not the whole forest interior or a claim about the precise legal boundary of a royal forest.
The willow trees beside the stream, source osiers. Reviewed native willow category; no exact modern botanical species is assigned, and the rank is a row, not social status.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: soft + green + cover

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: soft + green + cover
lexicon.label: moss_growth

senses.definition: Moss growing over the old oak’s branches. Native soft-green-cover as a lexicalized plant category; not any green cloth or all plants.
Wearing torn or worn clothing, the ragged sleeping man. Native rag form used adjectivally; not a change to his identity or the source’s account of how he arrived.
Bare of hair or its figurative leafy counterpart on the oak’s high top. Native hairless expression; the tree metaphor is preserved without diagnosing disease.
The milk-bearing breast of an animal, here the lioness’s drawn-dry udders. Native milk-breast; the source plural is retained without supplying an anatomical count.
Female lion in Oliver’s rescue story, native female + lion. Hunger and nursing state are stated separately; no substitution of a male lion.
Work food with the mouth, native mouth-crush, used metaphorically for Orlando considering sweet and bitter fancy. Not an assertion that he was actually eating.
A change of character or moral disposition, Oliver’s claimed conversion. Native change as a nominal sense; no unstated baptism, creed or separate new person is invented.

Warranted or rightful, especially a justified cause for resentment or redress. Native right used as an evaluative modifier, not merely/only, a mechanical direction or a claim that revenge is actually carried out.
A figure of speech or illustrative comparison in Touchstone’s deliberately pretentious lesson. Native speech-image; not a numeric figure, bodily shape or claim that his argument is valid.
A threatened beating with a stick, native stick-beat. No exact count of blows, target body part or actual attack is inserted into the comic threat.
A partisan group brought into a quarrel, the threatened bandying in faction. Native divided-party sense; no modern political institution or new group appearing onstage.

Outside the speaker’s Christian religious tradition, as Touchstone labels the unnamed philosopher. Native outside-people expression reviewed for this new source; not an imported Israel-versus-neighbours reference or the translator’s disparagement.

Middling or adequate, a colloquial repeated native so expression authored for William’s uncertain wealth and Touchstone’s reply. The repeated so stem also permits the echo of exactly so; this local idiom is a declared adaptation, not independent attestation of the source English pun.
Formal life-cessation expression opposed to the plain die in Touchstone’s glossing threat. Native life + cease; a later literary register variant, not an assertion of a different biological event.

lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_bfa_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 150; Unta 106.
A support suspending an injured arm, native arm-hang. Distinct from the stone-throwing weapon; no modern medical construction or treatment instructions are inserted.
The cloth used as an arm support in Rosalind’s heart-in-a-scarf joke. Native scarf form with this explicitly contextual use; not a new military badge or wound on the heart.

A practitioner of purported magical arts in Rosalind’s claimed acquaintance and self-description. Reviewed native specialist name, without the historical court context, asserted real efficacy or automatic condemnation.
A step in a flight of stairs, native up-step, extended to successive courtship stages. Source pair of stairs denotes a flight, not two staircases or a supplied exact tread count.

citations.locator: Authored native compound: land + right + give

lexicon.etymology: Authored native compound: land + right + give
lexicon.label: estate_settle

senses.definition: Bestow property or its rights as an estate upon another, source estate upon you. Native land-right-give; not merely social rank or a change in who physically occupies a house.
Headlong dizzying haste, native head-turn as a figurative motion expression. Oliver lists it among objections to sudden courtship; not a diagnosed illness or merely changing direction.
Devoted respectful attendance or service to the beloved. Nominal native attend, with both source occurrences retained; not a calendar observance or the editor’s substituted obedience.
Hurtful discourtesy or rough treatment, Phoebe’s complaint about disclosure of her letter. Nominal native rude; not merely low social rank or the physical texture of an object.
Clear the throat noisily before singing; not hunt with a falcon.
Rye as the cereal in the lovers’ field. Authored winter-grain lexical category, not an assertion that all winter grain is rye.
A field strip or cultivated plot in the song. No exact acreage is stated; not a forced modern area conversion.

The people called gypsies in the source comparison. Authored native ethnonym wander-people for this source-cultural referent, not a claim that all Romani travel or that every traveller is Romani. Source ethnonym and its outsider stereotype remain documented.
The Noah flood vessel in Jaques’s mock paired-animals allusion; not the covenant chest.
Account or judge something to be so, including reckoning the song wasted time. Not a noble count.
Facial appearance, source favor, by which Duke Senior recognizes his daughter; not kindness.
First principles of a discipline, not an asserted Unta ordinal in the source.
A defence establishing innocence or truth of a claim, Touchstone’s demand to prove courtier status. Not a medical purge.
A measured court dance; explicit metrical/dance extension of native measure retains the later measures/measure echo.
Full of pointed maxims or wise-seeming sayings; the Duke’s assessment of Touchstone.
The blunt short arrow of the fool’s-bolt proverb, not a door fastener.
An ailment in the source deliberately odd dulcet diseases phrase; do not silently emend to phrases.
An answering turn in the parody of quarrel etiquette.
A pointed mocking reply in Touchstone’s named ladder of quarrels.
An explicit rebuke within the escalating quarrel.
A countering rebuke, distinct in the named ladder from the preceding reproof.

citations.locator: Authored native derivation/sense: peace + make + person

lexicon.etymology: Authored native derivation/sense: peace + make + person
lexicon.label: peacemaker_person

senses.definition: An agent of reconciliation, here the quoted conditional if personified.
A horse or horse-shaped cover used to approach quarry unseen; the Duke’s metaphor for wit concealed by folly.
A dining board, hence shared sustenance in board and bed; not a writing tablet.
Fill a place with inhabitants, the song’s claim that marriage populates towns.
A brother’s daughter, here Duke Senior’s niece Celia; not his literal daughter or a claim that sister’s daughters are excluded from the broader kinship category.
The branch or bush displayed to advertise wine, the epilogue’s proverbial sign; not an unspecified plant growing in the wine.
Smile in a self-conscious or affected manner in the epilogue’s audience teasing.
A bending-knee gesture of courtesy closing the epilogue; not an archery bow.
The personified classical wedding god in the final masque, not an anatomical noun.
Full source personal name of the second brother, distinct from the melancholy courtier. No identity suffix is printed.
Authored native performance syllables for the song’s hey refrain; not a lexical translation or historical attestation.
Authored contrasting native performance syllables for ho; not an ordinary borrowed English word.
Authored expanded native refrain corresponding to hey-nonny-no.
Authored ringing performance refrain corresponding to the bird-song line; no claim of identical English metre.
Giving someone the lie: an accusation that they speak falsely. This is not a lie told by the accuser; qualified/direct are stages in Touchstone’s quarrel parody.
A pearl-bearing bivalve, lexicalized native pearl-cover, in the fair-pearl/foul-oyster contrast. Not every protective shell or a claim that every oyster contains a pearl.
Adopt a religious life and turn away from a former enterprise; Frederick’s reported conversion, without specifying an unprinted denomination.
Assign or leave a possession/status to someone, here a living duke renouncing power and Jaques assigning futures. Does not assert either speaker’s death.

lexicon.etymology: Origins_3_Unta_2 chart and explicit quantitative construction; Chart-2 cardinal; productive ordinal/multiple morphology where marked
lexicon.label: unta_times_h_over_b

senses.definition: Exact times quantity 7; Unta 7.
A formal spoken greeting, paired with ordinary greeting in Touchstone’s affected entrance.
A person or relation allied through shared interests, including the marriage connections promised to Oliver; not a claim of an actual military treaty.
A party to a quarrel in the etiquette anecdote, not a political faction or festive gathering.
Gather into a heap, used figuratively of overflowing joy at the final dance.
Provision with food for a journey, Jaques’s metaphor for a short-lived marriage.
A member of Rome’s hereditary patrician class in the play; native ancestry-noble, not every rich person or a modern political party.
The Roman governing council as represented in the drama. Distinct contextual institution from the historical Acts assembly; no modern elected chamber is substituted.
In rebellion against authority; the source stage description of armed citizens. This is not the translator endorsing either side’s claims about the famine.
Eat to excess, the citizens’ charge against those in authority. Not a count or a claim that all wealthy people literally ate the scene’s grain.
Fit or healthful to eat, before the rulers’ surplus spoils. The later wholesome-law sense is separately contextual.
Showing humane concern rather than merely belonging to the human species.
An itemized accounting of possessions, used of citizens’ leanness as proof of rulers’ abundance.
Specify item by item, the native part-name action in the inventory metaphor.
The long thrusting spear of the protestors, not the fish.
A toothed farm implement, used for the gaunt citizen’s shape. Native field-tooth category; not a libertine.
The ordinary citizen body in the political conflict, not an ethnic group.
The experience of deprivation and harm, nominal use of native suffer; not permission to act.
Bodily gauntness through hunger, not leaning or resting the body against something.
Greedily wanting wealth, the specific accusation the second citizen rejects in Martius’s case.
Talk idly or at excessive length, the first citizen’s impatient question before marching.
Scarcity of food in the city; not the ordinary desire/want verb.
A building storing supplies, the citizens’ accusation that stored grain is withheld. Reviewed promotion of the native historical category, not a modernization of any Bible file.
Ground grain, here the best nourishing portion in Menenius’s flour-versus-bran fable; not the flower.
The outer grain material separated in milling, contrasted with flour. Native grain-skin category, not a branch.
Remove a law’s force, the citizen’s charge that laws restraining the rich are repealed.
Beneficial or salutary when applied to a law, not literally safe to eat.
Make worn by repetition, Menenius’s deliberate retelling of a familiar story; not the direct food spoilage sense.
Put away food in storage, the accusation against the fable’s belly; not a new architectural room.
The body’s shared appetites or inclinations, broader than romantic love.
The constructed bodily frame in the political fable, not woven cloth.
A bodily defence or protective resource in the citizen’s list, not a documentary title deed.
Voracious like the proverbial bird, the citizen’s description of the belly. The bird image is explicitly recorded; native devouring epithet does not borrow the English animal sound.
A collecting drain or receptacle for bodily refuse, the citizen’s insult to the belly; native dirty-hole, not the act of sinking underwater.
An accounting of receipts and distributions, the belly’s claimed proof of fair provision.
A winding passage of the body in the fable, not a machine handle or an eccentric person.
Full source name of the Roman soldier who later receives Coriolanus; no unprinted identity suffix.
The same Caius Martius in shortened speaker/address form, not another Roman.
The older Roman interlocutor in Coriolanus, distinct from Antony and Cleopatra’s Agrippa.
Short source form of Menenius Agrippa, the belly-fable speaker.
The tribune in Coriolanus, distinct from Marcus Brutus in Julius Caesar; no role suffix appears in the name.
The tribune allied with Junius Brutus in this play; full source personal name.
The Roman commander in Coriolanus.
The Roman officer named in the source entrance.
The citizens’ collective assent to their proposal, using native judgment. The crowd borrows a judicial metaphor without becoming a legally constituted jury.
Material supplies beyond need, specifically the rulers’ alleged surplus food; no fixed numerical amount.
Costly to maintain, the hungry citizens’ bitter account of how their rulers value them; not affectionate dear.
Cause suffering, here hunger and gauntness harming the citizens; native torment extended without requiring deliberate torture.
The governed political community, not merely someone’s condition, and without imposing a modern nation-state or a particular constitution.
One connected component of a chain, the controlling links in the Roman-state metaphor.
Partial awareness or a hint of knowledge, without claiming exact prior knowledge of the citizens’ plan.
Carry someone away, physically or figuratively; calamity is the carrier in the opening political argument, not supernatural magic.
Await someone in the future, as further calamity threatens; not serving someone as an attendant.

lexicon.label: stave_club

senses.definition: A stout stick carried by the citizens, source bat; uses the native staff category, distinct in the paired list from the heavy club weapon. Not a flying animal or a modern sporting specification.
A prescribed public law in the citizens’ accusation about class oppression; distinct from a debt security.
A part or organ of the body in the political fable, not restricted to arms and legs.
Think out or contrive an action, the planning function among the body’s faculties.

lexicon.label: unta_cardinal_be_over_b

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 14; Unta 12.

The Roman civic garment worn for the consular petition, source toge. Native citizen-gown names its institutional category without importing an ordinary foreign word or specifying an unattested cut.
Given indiscriminately to everyone, the source common in my love. Retains the connection to sharing and the common people; does not introduce a sexual promiscuity claim.
Seeking favor through a gesture, source insinuating nod. The practiced deference is explicitly counterfeit in Coriolanus’s own speech.
A citizen’s assurance or endorsement of the candidate, source vouches. Explicit nominal use of native vouch; no written certificate or additional formal office is invented.
The stock familiar personal name in Hob and Dick, representing ordinary petitioned people rather than two newly introduced named characters. Phonetic personal-name adaptation only.
The stock familiar personal name paired with Hob; not an anatomical term, office or a new citizen identity. Phonetic personal-name adaptation only.
The marks of public office worn after selection, source official marks. Native office-mark; distinct from bodily wounds as marks of merit and without inventing particular insignia.
A binding term or stipulation imposed upon the candidate, source article tying him to aught. Neither a grammatical article nor a newspaper piece.
The civic body and its government, source state or weal. Distinct from an enduring condition and from one person’s landed estate; no modern national boundaries are asserted.

The Roman magistracy named in the ancestry speech as Censorinus’s twice-held office. Native citizen-judge identifies this civic office; not suppression of a text or an assertion that these events precede the dramatic action historically.
A guarantee of protected passage, source on safeguard during Aufidius’s meeting with Lartius. Not a personal guard soldier or an unmentioned written passport.
The former king claimed as part of Coriolanus’s family ancestry in Brutus’s speech. Full source name, distinct from the current Caius Martius.
Numa, maternal grandfather of Ancus in the ancestry claim; no other Numa is silently imported.
The king preceding Ancus in Brutus’s speech. Retain the source’s short Hostilius rather than adding an unprinted given name.
Publius of the Martian family in the source’s water-conduit ancestry claim, distinct from other Publii in later plays. No invented surname prints.
Quintus paired with Publius in Brutus’s ancestry claim. Personal name, not a number word to be converted to Unta five.
The named great ancestor in the supplied genealogy. Preserve the source’s explanation by the twice-held censor office without rewriting its historical chronology.
The city to which Aufidius has retired, distinct from the collective people of Antium. Geographic phonetic adaptation with no ordinary-word borrowing.
Hostile feeling, explicit nominal use of native hate in the tribunes’ accusations and Aufidius’s rivalry. It is attributed to the named speaker or reported person, not adopted as narrative judgment.
Capacity or tolerance for bearing something, source noble sufferance. Explicit nominal endure; neither a command to suffer nor a claim that the nobles must approve.
Awareness or apprehension of current behavior, source apprehension of his portance. Explicit nominal perceive, not anxiety or physical arrest.
Something obstructing the intended action, source impediment in the account the tribunes propose. Explicit nominal hinder without inventing a particular obstruction.
Stress or press a point in argument, source enforce his pride. Native strong-say rather than physical enforcement of the emotion.
Receive or add a further identifying name, source so surnamed Censorinus. Reviewed native name-add; not an assertion of a modern inherited surname convention.
Make a hostile incursion, source make road upon us. Reviewed native strike-enter; distinct from building or traveling a road.
The unwanted corn-field weed in Coriolanus’s metaphor for rebellion; reviewed native plant category, not shellfish. No modern species identification is imposed.
Political discord or incited rebellion in Coriolanus’s accusation. Reviewed native rebel-stir; the accusation belongs to the character, not the narrator.
Mint or produce as coins, figuratively lungs issuing words. Native coin-make keeps the monetary production image; not literal metal forming in the body.
Cover with scabs in the hostile disease metaphor for the common people; native scab-cover. No clinical diagnosis or new literal disease event is asserted.

senses.definition: A person currying favor with the current age or prevailing power, source timepleaser; not one entertaining clock-time or giving a numerical time reading.

Put seed into soil for a crop, reviewed native sow in the rebellion-as-weed metaphor. Distinct from planting a grown plant and from the following scattering action; no physical planting scene is added.
An authoritative rule invoked by Cominius after the tribune’s shall; native law sense. The English canon/cannon resonance is documented but no shared Vayrshemon sound is falsely claimed.
The Roman civic officer serving in the public-order and arrest scene. Native city-officer distinguishes the institution from a tribune or senator without importing the Latin office-name sound.
The named sea deity in the mocking Triton of minnows comparison. Not a creature-class word for a newt, and no literal divine identity is assigned to Sicinius.
The named many-headed mythic monster used for the common multitude. Proper-name adaptation; no exact head count is supplied or invented.
The little fish under the mock Triton’s rule, native small-fish category. Preserves the scale contrast without claiming a modern taxonomic species.
The bodily navel, reviewed native belly-mark, figuratively the state’s vital center under threat. No new anatomical injury or city location is invented.
Flavour perceived by taste, explicit nominal native taste in the blended-voices comparison. The dominant flavor of the mixture represents the commoners’ influence, not a literal meal.

citations.locator: Authored citation construction from native be:must; external nominal marking applies to the quoted predicate as a whole.

lexicon.etymology: Authored citation construction from native be:must; external nominal marking applies to the quoted predicate as a whole.
lexicon.label: obligation_citation

senses.definition: Metalinguistic citation of native be-with-obligation, used for the commanding shall discussed in Coriolanus3.1. The native predicate supplies a host for the bound modal; the quoted whole may take external nominal possession/case. It is not an English loan or a claim that the modal suffix is independently a free word.
A person attempting political change in Sicinius’s treason charge. Native change-person; not a modern technological entrepreneur and not a narrator verdict of guilt.
The animal in Coriolanus’s old-goat insult to Sicinius; reviewed native animal root, not a literal transformation or a new goat character.
Tear or cut destructively, figuratively dishonor mangling judgment. Native cut-break distinguishes the action from a tear shed by the eye.
A freedom or civic liberty the people are warned they may lose; native free as a noun. Distinct from personal licence and from a newly asserted modern constitutional guarantee.

A holder of civic governing authority, here the elected tribunes naming themselves the people’s magistrates. Native rule-officer; not a modern specialist court judge or a new office different from their tribunate.
Ignite or stir fire, metaphorically inflame political anger. Reviewed native fire-kindling sense; distinct from lighting a particular lamp.
Restrained and measured in proceeding, Menenius’s contrast with violent redress. Native restrained-gentle; not an assertion about climate or bodily temperature.
A piled mass, paired with heaps in the imagined destruction of the city. The mound sense, distinct from raised textile nap, preserves the deliberate near-synonym without inventing a quantity.
The proper geographic designation of Rome’s Tarpeian rock in the threatened execution. Used with the native word for rock; no unrelated person, modern location or extra victim is invented.

An uncivilized outsider in Coriolanus’s hostile denial that the commoners are true Romans. Native wild-person preserves his insult; not a neutral ethnic classification or a translator assertion that the people are less human.

A person of Rome in the contested civic identity of this play. The permitted place-name plus native person retains the designation without importing the later imperial setting or claiming a particular legal citizenship test.
Bear young as an animal, Coriolanus’s dehumanizing littered metaphor. Native beast-birth keeps the animal comparison without adding a literal dog birth, rubbish or a carrying vehicle.
Give birth to a calf, used as a hostile metaphor for the people’s Roman birth. Native calf-birth; not the mistaken action of carrying a burden.
The entrance space of the named Capitol in the civic-birth insult. Reviewed native door-place; no modern architectural plan is imposed.
Numerical reckoning in the claim that the hostile odds exceed calculation. Native measure-reckon names the discipline; no unstated count or decimal system is substituted for Unta.
Repair with a patch, used of the political breach that must be mended with cloth of any color. Native patch-make preserves the textile expedient and does not assert literal sewing in the scene.
A venomous snake in Sicinius’s accusation against Coriolanus. Reviewed native poison-serpent; no actual transformation or modern species identification is asserted.
Harshness or rigor of public power in Sicinius’s demand for summary punishment. Explicit nominal harsh, not a narrator endorsement of the sentence.
An imbalance of numbers favoring the opposing crowd, described as beyond arithmetic. Native number-excess retains the numerical comparison without inventing a ratio or betting probability.
Foolish conduct, explicit nominal fool in the warning that bravery against a falling structure is folly. Not a new court fool or a claim that the danger is theatrical entertainment.
Unrestrained slaughter signalled by the cry havoc, opposed to bounded lawful pursuit. Explicit nominal slaughter; no actual massacre is added to the scene.
Authority or permission limited by law, source modest warrant. Native law-permission, distinct from the verb guarantee and without inventing a written document.
The regular course of legal proceedings, urged instead of summary force. Native law-process; not a generic task workflow or a promise that the tribunal is impartial.

citations.locator: Authored native derivation/sense: small + weight + measure

lexicon.etymology: Authored native derivation/sense: small + weight + measure

senses.definition: The source ounce as a small historical weight unit in many an ounce of blood. A native measure-category label, not the feline ounce, a fluid-volume claim, or an assumed conversion between Roman, troy and avoirdupois standards. No exact number of ounces is supplied.
The source pound-weight in imagined leaden restraints on haste. Reviewed native weight category, not money or a verb of beating; no number of pounds or weight-standard conversion is invented.
Become gangrenous in the diseased-foot analogy. Native flesh-decay preserves the medical image; it is neither a diagnosis of Coriolanus nor medical advice.
An enduring mark of disgrace, figuratively a burned brand left on those who kill or permit the killing of their defender. Explicit nominal brand; not a new product label or actual branding scene.
The imagined downward fall from the heightened Tarpeian rock, source precipitation. Native down-fall; not rainfall or an assertion that any execution has occurred.
The textile material in woolen vassals, retaining the class-marking clothing and sheep association without changing the people into animals.
A contemptuously subordinated person in Coriolanus’s account of his mother’s woolen-vassal language. Native serve-person; the Roman setting is not made into a newly specified feudal contract.
An assembled public gathering, source congregations; not a specifically Christian congregation or an invented building.
Open the mouth in yawning, in Coriolanus’s contemptuous picture of the passive public. Native mouth-open lexicalized for this action; not an added spoken protest.
A violent attack or convulsive episode used as an image for the political crisis. Native violent-illness; not suitedness and not a diagnosis of an actual person.
Unbending or uncompromising in character, Volumnia’s too absolute. Native bend-lack; not total numerical completeness or a formal doctrine of absolute monarchy.
Commit words to the tongue by rote, as distinct from the heart’s endorsement of them. Native rote-learn; preserves the supplied roted reading without silently emending it to botanical rooted.
Acknowledgement or approval by the inner convictions, source allowance to the bosom’s truth. Explicit nominal approve; not an assigned allowance of money or food.
A boor in the speaker’s contemptuous reference to the public. Native rude-person; no unmentioned ethnic, medical or educational classification is imposed.
Contact or manipulation by the hand, which the fully ripe mulberry cannot withstand. Native hand-touch; not governing a political issue or an invented injury.
Shape or adjust oneself or one’s disposition to the required conduct. Native fit-make; neither an editor text frame nor the fabrication of a criminal charge.
Composure as a possible defense against the crowd, explicit nominal calm. It is offered as a course of action, not asserted to be Coriolanus’s present temperament.
The sex-worker spirit invoked in Coriolanus’s contemptuous fantasy of self-transformation. Reviewed native person category, not the verb prostitute and not a narrator judgment of any actual woman.
A boy attending school in the imagined weeping-schoolboy comparison. Native school-boy; no actual pupil is added to the stage.

A Roman civic grouping used to organize the citizens and their votes. Native citizen-group, not a newly asserted kinship lineage; the source supplies no number of tribes.
A monetary penalty among the proposed sentences, native money-penalty. Distinct from fine quality or thinness; no unstated amount or denomination is invented.
The longstanding civic entitlement invoked by the tribunes, native old-right. Their assertion of the right is not translator certification of the proceeding’s justice.
Spoken opposition in Brutus’s description of Coriolanus having his full portion of contradiction. Native against-say; preserves the supplied worth reading rather than silently emending it to word.

The bodily region named as the source of offspring in Cominius’s family-value comparison. Reviewed native body term, without inventing another child beyond the source.
Wet marshland in the rotten-fen comparison. Reviewed native wet-land; not a named place or a newly specified disease source.
An offensive smell or vapor in Coriolanus’s insult to the crowd, explicit nominal stink. Not narrator confirmation that the citizens carry a disease.

senses.definition: Exact cardinal quantity 20000000; Unta 68460A8.
An instructive principle remembered from Volumnia’s upbringing of her son. Native teach-rule, not a newly enacted civic statute.
Permission to return from banishment, source repeal in Cominius’s proposed plan. Native return-permit; distinct from remembering something or repealing an unspecified law.
Something witnessed, particularly the hardening sights of war. Explicit nominal sight; not eyeglasses, an added stage pageant, or a medical finding.
Foxlike craftiness in Volumnia’s accusation against the tribune. Native fox-cunning retains the animal image without asserting a literal transformation.
A test of metal’s quality, the figurative noble touch of trustworthy friends. Native metal-test retains the testing/purity image; not mere bodily contact or the fool Touchstone’s personal name.
Weak plaintive crying contrasted with Volumnia’s angry lament. Native faint-cry keeps her contemptuous characterization without a medical or moral judgment from the narrator.
Enter names separately in a military list, source distinctly billeted. Native name-write; does not assume the troops are assigned lodgings in this passage.
A cooking rod imagined as a weapon in the widows’ revenge. Native roast-rod; distinct from expelling saliva.
The household gatekeeper whom the servants accuse of admitting an unwelcome stranger. Native gate-guard; not a baggage carrier or a new named character.
The Roman informant in Coriolanus4.3, not the separately retained biblical Nicanor; no identity suffix prints.
The Volscian contact in Coriolanus4.3; distinct semantic identity from any other play’s Adrian, with no role appended to the printed name.
The servant called in Aufidius’s household, as named in the supplied source; no invented biography or role suffix in the proper form.
Place of one’s birth, Rome in Coriolanus’s reversal of civic attachment. Native birth-place; not necessarily the particular building or bed in which birth happened.
Unstable and liable to slip, figuratively the world’s reversals of friendship and enmity. Native slip as a modifier; no claim that an actual floor is wet.
A disagreement or quarrel that can rupture friendship over a tiny coin. Explicit nominal disagree; no unstated sum is assigned to the dispute.

The treatment given to an arriving person, source entertainment in Coriolanus’s judgment of his unwelcome arrival. Native receive-treat; distinct from amusement and from military employment in the previous scene.
The domestic fireplace or fire-floor where the stranger asks to stand. Reviewed native historical hearth; not the whole home or the host’s heart.
A jackdaw in the servant’s bird-city retort, native small-crow. Also available as a contemptuous fool image in this exchange; not a personal name or an invented precise zoological claim.

The overhead canopy as an evasive image for the sky/open world. Explicit figurative extension of the inherited native canopy; leaves the bird-city reply unlocalized instead of replacing it with a specific city.

Interfere with or concern oneself with a person, with sexual involvement evoked by the answering mistress clause. Explicit contextual extension of native interfere; preserves the repeated verb without asserting that an affair actually happened.
A face-wrapping garment removed when Coriolanus identifies himself. Reviewed native face-wrap; neither an engine device nor a gag.
A ship’s rope equipment, source torn tackle as an image for the stranger’s ragged clothes. Native ship-rope; the noble vessel is a ship, not merely a container.
Diseased or corrupted, applied to the speaker’s country; native illness-rot. Distinct from the earlier flower-eating canker caterpillar and not a medical diagnosis of the people.
Furious anger in Coriolanus’s promise to fight with infernal spite. Explicit nominal native fury; preserves the emotional force while documenting the loss of the source bodily-humour image.

senses.definition: A large cask or source volume category, hyperbolically filled with blood. Native great-wine-vessel names the cask capacity image; no fixed gallon conversion, number of tuns, or weight in tons is asserted.
A spear of ash wood, source ash as the weapon that breaks against Martius. Reviewed native tree-kind plus spear; not burnt ash or an unsupported precise modern botanical identification.
The fibrous pattern or grain of wood, source grained ash. Native wood-line, distinct from cereal grain and the scarlet grain dye.
A sharp fragment of broken wood, in the exaggerated image of spear splinters scarring the moon. Native wood-fragment; not an actual astronomical event.
The metalworking support figuratively identified with the opponent’s body enduring sword blows. Reviewed native metal-hold; not an anatomical object.
Muscular flesh, especially the arm bearing the shield that Aufidius intended to hew away. Native strong-flesh, not prepared meat or a target board.
Military command/authority offered in equal shares to the former opponent. Native army-authority; distinct from a sales fee or an unspecified written letter.
A heavy stick invoked in the servant’s boast about striking the stranger. Native heavy-rod; a contemplated blow, not a newly performed assault.
A spinning toy set moving by the fingers in the servant’s comparison. Native turn-play; not the highest point or a ranking.

An earned additional identifying name, specifically Coriolanus alongside Caius Martius. Native name-add used nominally; not an assertion of a hereditary surname.
Harm or destructive wrongdoing acknowledged toward the Volsces. Reviewed native evil-work, not harmless play or a modern misdemeanor category.
Chop or cut forcefully, applied to a shield carried on the arm. Reviewed native cutting action, without restricting the shield material to wood.

The thumb paired with a finger in the spinning-top comparison. Reviewed native bodily term; no hand deformity or actual number of fingers is supplied.
Cut a notch or score, paired with scotch/cut in the servants’ meat comparison. Native cut-mark; not a numerical score or tally.
Meat slashed for grilling, the image for Aufidius’s wounds. Native grill-flesh; retains the cooking comparison without importing the dish-name sound.

citations.locator: Authored native derivation/sense: credit + straight + state

lexicon.etymology: Authored native derivation/sense: credit + straight + state
lexicon.label: directitude_blunder

senses.definition: An intentionally ill-fitting learned-sounding native compound, credit-straight-state, for the servant’s directitude. Context suggests discredit/disgrace but the source sense is uncertain; the next speaker repeats and questions it. This is an authored compensating joke, not an ordinary synonym or an exact phonetic reproduction of the English pun.
A disabling bodily shutdown or torpor in the servant’s personification of peace. Native body-stop, without imposing a modern clinical diagnosis or cause.
Heavy unresponsive drowsiness in the hostile description of peace. Native heavy-sleep; distinct from healthy ordinary sleep or a moral judgment by the narrator.

citations.locator: Authored native derivation/sense: drink + life + lack

lexicon.etymology: Authored native derivation/sense: drink + life + lack
lexicon.label: mulled_flat

senses.definition: Lifeless/flat as exhausted drink, source mulled in the peace metaphor. Native drink-life-lack; not a recipe for warmed spiced wine. The opposed vigor is retained without claiming one uncontested etymology for vent.
Lacking sensation or responsiveness in the personification of peace. Native sense-lack; not simply imprudent or an actual diagnosis of a person.
A perpetrator of sexual violence, in the servingman’s personification of war. Native ravish-person preserves the opposed sexual injury and cuckold-making analogy; it is not merely a destroyer.
An animal’s hole in the ground, the rabbits’ refuge in the servant’s image for Coriolanus’s concealed supporters. Native earth-hole, not a named place.
Lively force in the praise of war, source full of vent. Native life-strength; preserves energetic force without deciding between disputed hunting and drink associations in the source word.
Accommodate one’s conduct to the circumstances of the time. Native time-yield; Menenius imagines the outcome if Coriolanus could have done this, not a claim that he did or merely delayed.
Disrespectfully overbearing, in Brutus’s judgment of Coriolanus. Native respect-lack, distinguished from courage, pride alone or a narrator’s verdict.
Masonry-binding material, in the predicted burning of Roman temples down into their cement. Native stone-bind; not a modern Portland-cement formulation or an emended encircling wall.
A hole-boring tool, source auger in the image of public rights compressed into its narrow bore. Native bore-tool, without an invented diameter or numeral.

A fool’s head in Menenius’s threat that heads will fall as caps once flew. Native fool-head preserves the contempt and cap/head parallel, without inventing literal cock feathers or a separate jester costume.
Enchanting craft as an image for Coriolanus’s hold on the soldiers. Native enchant-craft; the lieutenant expresses wonder, not proof that literal magic has been performed.
A blessing or grace before food. Native meal-blessing preserves the soldiers’ quasi-sacred admiration without borrowing a foreign religious formula.
Prudent management or stewardship, here of the Volscian polity. Native house-manage used nominally; not marital conduct or literal farming.

The fish-taking hawk in Aufidius’s image of natural dominance. Native fish-hawk; preserves the source animal category and its attributed sovereignty without claiming the literary fascination belief as zoological fact.
Light grain husks, in the contrast between Coriolanus’s few friends and the disliked population. Reviewed native grain-husk category, not cut stalk stubble; the contempt belongs to the characters.

The figurative pipes and conveyances of blood in Menenius’s account of hunger and persuasion. Native blood plus hollow passage; preserves the speaker’s historical physiology without asserting it as modern medical fact.
An individual cereal kernel, contrasted with chaff in the few-friends metaphor. Explicit counted use of native kernel, distinct from collective corn, grain dye and wood grain.
A small separate portion of liquid, here the blood shed together by comrades. Explicit nominal use of native drop, not the falling action, an imposed volume unit or an eye-tear.
Make a low nonverbal dismissive sound at a petitioner, source Coriolanus humming at Cominius. Contextual extension of native hum; no song, tune or accompaniment is asserted.
The source pint as a liquid-volume unit in the guard’s threat to shed blood. Native cup-measure names the unit. Its historical size is left unspecified.
The rolling ball in the game of bowls. Menenius imagines his praise overrunning its intended mark on a deceptive playing surface.
Weak or shaking in the watchman’s contemptuous image of an elderly intercessor. The charge belongs to the speaker.
Give a statement the authority of a seal. Menenius says he almost gave a falsehood currency by praising his friend.
A small heap made by a burrowing mole. Its contrast with Olympus expresses the enormity of a mother bowing to her son.
A young goose imagined as following instinct in Coriolanus’s attempt to disown family feeling.
Work over ploughed earth. The passage imagines Italy treated as a field after Rome is ploughed.
A pendant formation of ice in the image of chastity at Dian’s temple.
A conspicuous object guiding mariners. The blessing likens a boy who will guide soldiers through peril to a mark surviving gusts at sea.
Sulfur in the image of a thunderbolt charged with force yet restrained to split an oak.
The offspring of a sitting hen. Volumnia identifies her son as the brood to which she gave all her care.
The hen’s call to her brood, applied to Volumnia sending her son to war and welcoming him home.
The child of Coriolanus and Virgilia and the grandchild of Volumnia. Young and boy remain separate descriptive words wherever supplied.
The Publicola identified here by his sister Valeria. This source supplies no identification with the naval officer in Antony and Cleopatra.
The named mountain imagined inclining in supplication before a molehill.
Flick or strike lightly with the finger. In the impossible image pebbles would flick the stars.
A writer or originating maker. Coriolanus imagines a man as author of his own existence.
A diplomatic mission bringing a public request or proposing terms. The collective mission can include multiple messengers.
An insect in its immature form, paired with the butterfly in the speaker’s comparison of a man becoming a dragon.
Armour protecting the torso that the warrior’s gaze could pierce in Menenius’s exaggeration.
A battering assault upon a fortification. Menenius hears the warrior’s low hum as a powerful attack.

A resonant struck metal plate in the procession’s percussion.

Hatch or bring young from eggs,egg-open;the nesting bird action inIsaiah34:15. Distinct from opening an arbitrary container or a nautical hatch;no exact egg count or incubation procedure added.
Soap,the cleansing substance paired with nitre,wash-matter. Keeps the supplied historical label distinct from the mineral without asserting a chemical formula or recipe.
A written portion or leaf of the roll inJeremiah36:23,scroll-part. Retains the source reading-unit without asserting a modern bound page or a botanical leaf.

Rabsaris,the printed Babylonian official designation inJeremiah39;kept beside named officials without asserting identity with the earlier Assyrian bearer. Supplied local relationship retained without invented etymology, namesake merger or outside harmonization.

Spread or smear a coating on a surface,the source wall-daubing action; spread-plaster. Does not certify sound construction or replace the specified coating with modern plaster chemistry.

A navigator or guiding officer of a ship,ship-guide;source pilot,distinct from the general sailor and from an aircraft pilot.
Close or seal a vessel's seams against water,ship-close;the source calking trade without specifying a modern sealant or construction method. Agent derivation names a calker.

Melzar,the supplied designation of the keeper over Daniel and his three companions;no assertion here about name versus historical title. Supplied local relationship retained without invented etymology, namesake merger or outside harmonization.

Baptize:the source ritual washing,water-wash-set-apart. Retains baptism as its named act without specifying an unprinted mode of immersion or sprinkling;Spirit/fire uses remain the source's extensions of this same verb.
Gospel,the proclaimed good news of the kingdom in Matthew4:23;good-news. Not automatically a title of a completed written book.
Lunatick,the historical lunar-illness label in Matthew4:24. Retains the source category without asserting lunar causation or retrospectively diagnosing epilepsy or a psychiatric condition.
Jonas,the supplied Gospel form in Matthew12's prophetic comparison;inherits Jonah's name-form but does not revise the frozen Jonah text or substitute Matthew's whale wording into it.

Crow,the male chicken's call in Matthew26 denial narrative;cock-cry,distinct from the existing crow bird noun. The printed before-crow/three-denials sequence is not altered to another Gospel's counting.

The hinder part or stern of the ship in Mark4:38,ship-behind;distinct from rear meaning upbringing or stern meaning severity. No unprinted boat design is asserted.

James,the brother specifying Judas in Luke6:16. The local relation is retained without an unprinted identification with Zebedee's or Alphaeus's son.

Towel in John13,wash-cloth,the cloth with which Jesus girds himself and wipes feet;no modern size,material or distinction between bathing accessories invented.
Anchor,a vessel-holding device in Acts27,ship-hold. Distinguished from a ships internal hold or an abstract source of emotional stability;no unprinted material or design supplied.

Quicksands,the feared unstable sands or sandy shipping hazard in Acts27:17,soft-sand. Preserves the source hazard label without imposing a modern dramatic sinking-pit mechanism or a substituted proper geographic name.
Rudder,the steering member of the ship in Acts27:40,ship-turn. The source plural bands are expressed separately;no modern single-stern-rudder design is asserted.
Creek,a coastal inlet with a shore in Acts27:39,sea-enter. Not automatically a small freshwater stream or an asserted named modern bay.
Boat,the subsidiary craft carried or towed with the main ship in Acts27,small-ship. Distinct from the main vessel and from the earlier river ferry;no exact size,capacity or hull design is added.

Shipwreck in2Corinthians11:25,ship-breaking or wrecking suffered by the speaker. The three occurrences are retained without identifying them with an unprinted voyage or treating the separately narrated Acts wreck as part of this count.
Evangelist in Ephesians4:11,a good-news proclaimer,gospel-person. Preserves a separate role beside apostle,prophet,pastor and teacher without inventing a modern denomination or numerical hierarchy.

Anchor of the soul in Hebrews6:19,hope as the holding-device image,sharing ship-hold. Explicit metaphorical extension of the actual nautical anchor;no literal vessel,anchor material or medical emotional-stability diagnosis is asserted.
